A camera that's removed falls back to the default camera, and when it comes back it's chosen again with its format. Plugging in or removing a device doesn't change what the panel remembers.
31	
32	### Record Into
33	
34	**Record Into** follows whichever project is in front, until you choose a row yourself. After that it keeps your choice for as long as that project stays open. When you press Record, the row freezes, so switching to another window during the recording doesn't change where the recording goes.
35	
36	### Paused recordings are stretches
37	
38	A pause ends the current file and a resume starts a new one, so a paused recording is several files, one for each stretch between a start or resume and a pause or the stop. Each file is named by the time its stretch began. When the recording lands, the stretches sit end to end on one track, touching, with no transition between them. Each stretch's microphone file goes on the Microphone track, lined up with its own picture.
39	
40	The paused time is in no file. The elapsed time counts only what was recorded.
41	
42	## Where it lands
43	
44	When you stop, the panel's button reads **Stopping…** and then **Adding…** while the files are written and imported.
45	
46	### Into an open project
47	
48	The recording goes into the project you chose in **Record Into**, at its playhead, in whatever container is open (inside a nest if you're working in one):
49	
50	- The picture goes on the front track if it fits there. If not, Frame Job adds a new track in front of everything.
51	- The microphone goes on a new back track named **Microphone**.
52	- Everything is one undo step, **Add Recording**. Undo removes the clips and media entries but leaves the files on disk, just as undoing Add Media… does.
53	- The new clips are selected.
54	
55	If you're in the middle of a drag in that project when the recording stops, Frame Job waits for the drag to end before adding the recording, for up to 20 seconds. After that it gives up, and the panel names the files, which are on disk either way.
56	
57	If the project you chose was closed while you were recording, the recording opens as a new project instead, and the panel says so.
58	
59	### As a new project
60	
61	With **Record Into** set to **New Project**, the recording opens as a new project. The project is named after the recording's file, for example `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22`, and that's the name Save offers. The canvas takes the movie's size and the frame rate you chose in **Rate**. The first stretch's picture is the project itself, so it has no undo step. Any later stretches, the microphone and a camera recorded beside the screen are added as one undo step: for a single stretch, **Add Microphone** with a microphone, **Add Camera** with a camera, or **Add Camera and Microphone** with both, and **Add Recording Segments** otherwise. A new project made from a recording is unsaved and asks before it closes.
62	
63	### Enhancing the microphone
64	
65	With **Enhance the microphone when it lands** ticked, the recording lands exactly as it would otherwise, and then Frame Job runs [Enhance Voice](audio.md#enhance-voice) on the microphone's clips: each stretch's microphone file, or a voice-over's files. It never touches the picture, a camera or the system audio. Enhance Voice needs the microphone's sound analysed first (its loudness and its speech), which takes a few seconds after the files land; it then runs under the **Measuring Sound** sheet, at Normalize's target loudness, and its settings appear in the clip's Sound tab.
66	
67	It's its own undo step, **Enhance Voice**, after the landing's. Edit ▸ Undo first reads **Undo Enhance Voice**, which takes the processing off and keeps the recording; in an open project the next undo is **Undo Add Recording**. In a new project the next is the landing's own step (**Add Microphone**, **Add Camera and Microphone** or **Add Recording Segments**), or nothing when the recording is a single file, which is the project itself.
68	
69	It waits while you drag in the project, while a sheet is up on its window, or while you're inside another nest than the one the recording landed in. Pressing **Cancel** on the Measuring Sound sheet leaves the clips as they landed. When there's nothing to enhance (a silent microphone, for example), or the sound wasn't analysed within 5 minutes, the reason appears at the foot of the inspector, and you can select the clip and choose **Clip ▸ Enhance Voice** yourself.
70	
71	### When it lands
72	
73	The three boxes under **When it lands:** polish a screen recording once it's in the project. The recording lands exactly as it would otherwise, any [Enhance the microphone](#enhancing-the-microphone) runs first, and then, in this order, each ticked box runs its command on the recording's screen clips (the clips of each stretch's movie that has a cursor file):
74	
75	1. **Zoom in on clicks** runs **Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…** with the values the Auto Zoom sheet last used, Zoom on typing on when the recording has typing.
76	2. **Show shortcuts** runs **Clip ▸ Add Shortcut Overlays** (bottom, dark).
77	3. **Speed up typing** runs **Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…** with the values its sheet last used, once the microphone's speech has been detected, so typing you talk over keeps its pace.
78	
79	Zooms are planned on the clips before the speed-up splits them, and the speed-up leaves each overlay at its pace. No sheet comes up. Each is its own undo step, **Auto Zoom**, **Add Shortcut Overlays** and **Speed Up Typing**, after the landing's (and after **Enhance Voice**), so Edit ▸ Undo takes them off one at a time, last first, and keeps the recording.
80	
81	Like Enhance, each waits while you drag in the project, while a sheet is up on its window, or while you're inside another nest than the one the recording landed in. When a command is refused, the reason appears at the foot of the inspector and the next one still runs; that includes a speed-up that would leave a clip silent above ×12, which this never applies without asking (choose **Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…** yourself to be asked). When the project stays busy, or the speech isn't detected, for 5 minutes, that is said there too and the rest don't run; select the clips and choose the command yourself. A recording with no cursor file, and a command with nothing to do (no click, no shortcut, no typing stretch long enough), change nothing and say nothing.
82	
83	Show shortcuts and Speed up typing need **Record shortcuts**: without it the cursor file holds no shortcut and no typing.
84	
85	### When the panel comes back
86	
87	A recording that lands cleanly doesn't bring the panel back. Press ⌥⌘N to open it again. The panel returns on its own, with a note, only when it was on screen when the recording began and there's something to say, for example:
88	
89	- the recording was stopped from macOS's indicator, or the display slept or went away, or the camera stopped on its own
90	- the project you chose had closed, so it opened as a new project
91	- a stretch's movie couldn't be read (for example an empty file from a pause right after a resume) and was left out. Its microphone file still lands on the Microphone track where the picture would have been, and the next picture starts after that gap. The note names the left-out file and the files it kept. Only a recording with no readable movie at all fails, and its note names every file.
92	- the files didn't finish writing within 10 s of Stop. The note reads "The recording did not finish writing within 10 s." and names the movie and microphone files kept on disk.
93	- the microphone stopped or failed (the picture still landed)
94	- a resume failed
95	- a file couldn't be placed and was added to the media list only
96	- the recording was saved but couldn't be added. The note reads "The recording was saved at … but could not be added: …" and names every file.
97	
98	## Files and formats
99	
100	Recordings are saved in **`~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/`**, which Frame Job creates the first time it's needed. They're never stored inside the project package. To carry them into the package, use Consolidate (see [Projects and media](projects-and-media.md)).
101	
102	| File | Name | Format |
103	|---|---|---|
104	| Screen recording | `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22.mov` | QuickTime movie, HEVC (H.264 where HEVC isn't available), with system audio as one stereo 48 kHz track when System Audio is on |
105	| Its microphone | `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22 (Microphone).m4a` | Mono 48 kHz AAC, beside the movie |
106	| Voice-over | `Voice-over 2026-10-02 at 09.15.04.m4a` | Mono 48 kHz AAC |
107	| Camera recording | `Camera Recording 2026-10-26 at 17.14.33.mov` | QuickTime movie at the camera's format, HEVC (H.264 where HEVC isn't available), no sound of its own; its microphone file sits beside it as for a screen recording |
108	| Its cursor | `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22.fjcursor` | Beside every screen recording's movie (a display, a window or a picked window), one per stretch between pauses: where the pointer was about 120 times a second, every click and scroll, and how the recorded area sat on the screen. With Cursor set to In the picture, the pointer is drawn into the movie as well. If the file can't be written, the recording still lands and the panel's note says why |
109	
110	When a name is already taken, Frame Job adds ` (2)`, ` (3)` and so on.
111	
112	The microphone is always a separate file from system audio, so you can set the level of your voice and the computer's sound independently. Frame Job measures how far apart the two files started and places the microphone clip to match, trimming its head if it started first.
113	
114	### Frame rate
115	
116	macOS delivers a new frame only when something on screen changes, so a mostly still screen gives a file with a low, uneven frame rate. That rate comes from the file itself and isn't a fault. The **Rate** setting is the most frames per second the file can hold. A new project uses that setting as its frame rate, while the media entry keeps the file's real rate. Where the picture stops changing before the sound ends, the last frame is held to the end of the clip.
117	
118	## The cursor
119	
120	A recording's cursor file (`<name>.fjcursor`, beside its movie) travels with the movie into your project:
121	
122	- **When a recording lands**, each stretch's movie gets its own cursor file.
123	- **When you import a movie**, by **File ▸ Add Media…**, a drop, opening it, or an agent's `import_media`, Frame Job looks beside it for a file with the same name ending in `.fjcursor`. It takes the file only when the file reads as a cursor file and was made for a movie of exactly this movie's size. A file that is missing, damaged or made for another size is left alone, and the movie imports without it. A copy Frame Job makes of a WebM or Matroska file is not looked beside.
124	- **When you relink a movie** (**Relink…**, the Media tab, or an agent's `relink_media`), Frame Job takes the cursor file beside the new movie. If there is none, it keeps the cursor file the media already had, as long as that file is still there and the new movie is the same size. Otherwise the media has no cursor file after the relink.
125	- **When you consolidate**, the cursor file is copied into the package beside its movie, and a moved package finds it there again (see [Consolidate Media](projects-and-media.md#consolidate-media)).
126	
127	**On the Media tab.** Select a recording in the list and its **Cursor** section names its cursor file, or says "No cursor file", or adds "— missing" when the file has gone. **Locate…** chooses a `.fjcursor` file for it: Frame Job takes it only when it reads as a cursor file made for a movie of exactly this size, and otherwise says why and changes nothing (undo name "Locate Cursor File"). **Remove** forgets the cursor file, which stays on disk (undo name "Remove Cursor File").
128	
129	*Agents:* `set_media_cursor` attaches, moves or removes a cursor file as **Locate…** and **Remove** do. `get_cursor_events` reads a recording's clicks, scrolls, shortcuts, typing stretches and pointer path, in the file's own time or in a clip's, with each click's place in the clip's zoom region frame.
130	
131	**The Cursor section.** A clip whose movie has a cursor file the picture doesn't already show gets a **Cursor** section on the Clip tab's **Picture** sub-tab, after **Background**. It starts closed; its summary says **off**, **on** or **arrow**, with **+ ripples** when clicks ripple. Each row is its own undo step:
132	
133	| Row | What it does | Range |
134	|---|---|---|
135	| **Show cursor** | Draws the pointer from the file over the clip. On by default. | on, off |
136	| **Size** | How big the pointer is drawn. Quick picks 50, 100, 150, 200 and 400 %; the slider runs to 400 %, the field to 800 %. | 25–800 % |
137	| **Style** | **As recorded** draws the pointer images the file recorded. **Arrow** draws Frame Job's own arrow instead. | As recorded, Arrow |
138	| **Smoothing** | Calms a shaky path. The pointer still passes exactly through every click, at the moment of the click, and still holds still where it held still. | Off, Light, Medium, Strong |
139	| **Hide when idle** | Fades the pointer out after this long with no movement or click, and brings it back just before it next moves. | Never, 1, 2, 3, 5, 10 s |
140	| **Clicks** | **Ripple** draws a ring growing out of every click. | None, Ripple |
141	| **Ripple color** | The ring's colour, with opacity. Live only while Clicks is Ripple. | any colour |
142	| **Ripple size** | How big the ring grows. Live only while Clicks is Ripple. | 25–400 % |
143	
144	**Polish** sets Smoothing to Medium and Hide when idle to 3 s in one step.
145	
146	With an action selected, **Size** and **Ripple size** animate across it. **Show cursor**, **Style**, **Clicks** and **Ripple color** switch at the action's end. **Smoothing**, **Hide when idle** and **Polish** belong to the clip, not to an action: their rows show ⊘ and they always change the clip itself. A clip with no cursor settings yet gets them the first time you change any row but Smoothing or Hide when idle with an action selected, so Size and Ripple size can animate rather than jump. Selecting clips that disagree shows a row mixed. **Reset** puts every row back to its default.
147	
148	**The arrow.** Frame Job's own arrow is drawn crisp at any size, at the size of a standard pointer times **Size**. It is also what a clip draws when its cursor file recorded no pointer images, whichever **Style** is chosen.
149	
150	**Paste Attributes** (⌥⌘V) carries a clip's cursor settings to another clip, with the rest of its picture settings.
151	
152	**Motion blur.** With the clip's **Motion Blur** above 0 (the Transform section, see [Motion blur](motion-and-transitions.md#motion-blur)), a moving pointer is drawn streaked along its path across the shutter, in the preview, `render_frame` and every export; a still pointer is drawn as it is. The click ripples stay sharp.
153	
154	**What a recording lands with.** With **Cursor** set to **Separate**, macOS draws no pointer into the movie, the cursor file says the pointer is not in the picture, and the landed clip gets a **Cursor** section, with the pointer drawn as recorded. With **Show Clicks** on as well, the clips land with **Clicks** set to **Ripple**, in the same undo step as the recording (in a new project whose only other change is that, the undo name is "Cursor Clicks"). Nothing else is set: **Polish** is one click away. With **In the picture**, the pointer is in the movie, its cursor file says so, and the clip shows no **Cursor** section, so nothing is drawn twice.
155	
156	### Shortcuts and Input Monitoring
157	
158	With **Record shortcuts** ticked, a display or window recording also writes your keyboard into each stretch's cursor file, in two kinds:
159	
160	- **A shortcut**, with its keys spelled out, for example `cmd+shift+4`. A key you press while holding ⌘ or ⌃ is a shortcut, and so is ⌥ with an arrow, Delete, Forward Delete, Return, Enter, Tab or Esc. ⇧ on its own never makes one, and neither does ⌥ with any other key (⌥E types é). The modifiers come first, in the order `cmd`, `ctrl`, `opt`, `shift`, then the key: a named key (`return`, `tab`, `space`, `left`, `f5` and so on) or the character the key types with no modifier, lowercased (`+` is spelled `plus`).
161	- **A typing mark**: the time of every other key you press, and of every key held down until it repeats. A typing mark never says which key it was. Frame Job doesn't read the character of a typed key at all.
162	
163	**Nothing is recorded while any app holds secure input**, as a password field does: not a shortcut, not even a typing mark. A password field that doesn't turn secure input on, such as a Terminal `sudo` prompt with **Secure Keyboard Entry** off, is recorded as typing marks only, with no characters. Keys pressed while the recording is paused aren't recorded.
164	
165	Recording keys needs macOS's **Input Monitoring** permission (see [Permissions](#permissions)). While it records, the menu-bar item shows the keyboard mark (see [The menu-bar item](#the-menu-bar-item)). *Agents:* `record_screen` with `keys: "shortcuts"`, and `get_cursor_events` reads the shortcuts and typing back.
166	
167	## Voice-overs (Microphone Only)
168	
169	To record narration over your edit, choose **Microphone Only** in **Source**:
170	
171	- **System Audio**, **Show Clicks**, **Size** and **Include Frame Job windows** grey out. Their values are kept for next time.
172	- **Rate** stays live, because it sets the rate of a new project. **Microphone** and **Record Into** stay live too.
173	- You must choose a microphone. With **Off**, Record says "Microphone Only records the microphone alone — choose a microphone first."
174	- Only the Microphone permission is checked. Screen Recording isn't needed.
175	
176	The countdown and the menu-bar item work as they do for a screen recording. Unlike a screen recording, **the panel stays up** while a voice-over records. Its controls lock, the meter stays live, the footnote shows ● or ❚❚ and the elapsed time, Record reads **Stop**, and a **Pause** / **Resume** button appears beside it. If you close the panel, the voice-over carries on. Stop it from the menu-bar item or **File ▸ Stop Recording** (⌥⌘N), and use the welcome window's **New Recording…** button to bring the panel back.
177	
178	Each stretch between pauses is its own `.m4a` file. In an open project, every file lands on a **new back track named Microphone**, end to end from the playhead, as one **Add Recording** undo step. It never goes on an existing track. As a new project, the first file is the project (1920×1080 at the chosen rate) and later files follow it on its one track.
179	
180	While a voice-over records, the panel's note shows a refused **Resume** as it happens: the reason appears there and the voice-over stays paused.
181	
182	If the microphone stops on its own (for example, it's unplugged), the voice-over ends there and what was recorded still lands, with a note.
183	
184	## Permissions
185	
186	A screen recording needs macOS's **Screen Recording** permission (**System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Screen & System Audio Recording**). A recording with a microphone, and every voice-over, also needs the **Microphone** permission (**System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Microphone**). A camera recording needs the **Camera** permission instead of Screen Recording, and a screen recording with **Record the camera too** needs both. Frame Job asks for each one when you press Record, before the countdown begins:
187	
188	- **Screen Recording.** The first press without it shows macOS's prompt, and the panel explains what to do. Once you've turned it on, relaunch Frame Job if macOS asks you to, then press Record again. Every later press without the permission opens System Settings at the right pane.
189	- **Microphone.** Asked only when a microphone is chosen. If you've never answered, macOS's prompt appears, and the countdown starts as soon as you allow it. If you denied it before, the press opens System Settings at the Microphone pane.
190	- **Input Monitoring.** Asked only with **Record shortcuts** ticked and a display or window as the source (**System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Input Monitoring**), after Screen Recording and before the camera and the microphone. macOS shows no prompt for it, and Frame Job isn't in that pane's list until you add it, so the first press both asks and opens System Settings at the Input Monitoring pane; the note says "Input Monitoring is not granted to Frame Job. Turn it on in System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Input Monitoring. If Frame Job is not in its list, add it with +." Turn Frame Job on there (add it with **+** if it isn't listed) and press Record again. Every later press without the permission opens the pane again. No relaunch is needed.
191	- **Camera.** Asked only with **Source** set to **Camera**, or with **Record the camera too** ticked (**System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Camera**), after Screen Recording when there is a screen and before the microphone. If you've never answered, macOS's prompt appears; allowing it goes on to the microphone and the countdown, and denying it leaves the panel idle with a note. If you denied it before, the press opens System Settings at the Camera pane and the note says so.
192	
193	While a system prompt or System Settings is up, the panel stops floating above other windows, so it doesn't cover them. It floats again on your next press of Record, or when the panel is opened again.
194	
195	If Frame Job was started from a terminal or another app rather than from the Finder or the Dock, macOS applies that app's permissions instead of Frame Job's. In that case the panel's note names the launching process (by its pid) and says to relaunch with `open -a "Frame Job"`, or to grant the permission to that app (the terminal, for a shell launch).
196	
197	## For agents: `record_screen`
198	
199	`record_screen` records for a fixed number of seconds, then lands the result exactly as the panel does: into the target project at its playhead, or as a new project when no project is open. A new project is named after the recording's file and is addressed as `project: <the recording's path>`, the path `get_project` reports for it.
200	
201	There's no countdown: the recording starts at once, and the call blocks for `seconds` plus about a second, returning once the recording is finished, imported and placed. Slow file writers can hold it up to about 75 s more, and 60 s more for each further stretch of a paused recording. A timeout names the movies, which may still finish on their own.
202	
203	| Argument | What it does | Default |
204	|---|---|---|
205	| `seconds` | How long to record, 1–600 s. Required. | — |
206	| `source` | `screen`, `voice_over` (the panel's Microphone Only) or `camera` (a camera on its own). | `screen` |
207	| `camera` | With `source: "camera"`, which camera: its unique id, or its name in any case. With `source: "screen"`, a camera to record beside the screen (below). | the default camera with `source: "camera"`; none with `source: "screen"` |

226	
227	With `source: "voice_over"`, the default microphone is implied. The arguments `display`, `window`, `system_audio`, `show_clicks`, `size`, `include_framejob_windows`, `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays`, `speed_up_typing`, `keys`, `cursor` and `microphone: false` are refused by name.
228	
229	With `source: "camera"`, Frame Job records a camera on its own, with no screen, into `Camera Recording <date> at <time>.mov`. The camera is the one `camera` names, or else the default camera: the Mac's preferred camera, then the first built-in camera, then the first one connected. It records at the camera's best format (the largest size wider than tall that runs at 30 fps or more, at that format's highest frame rate), or at the format `camera_format` names. A blank or null `camera_format` means best, and a format the camera doesn't have is refused with a list of the camera's formats. `microphone: true` adds the default microphone as a second file, as for a screen recording. The arguments `display`, `window`, `system_audio`, `show_clicks`, `size`, `include_framejob_windows`, `keys`, `cursor`, `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays`, `speed_up_typing` and `rate` are refused by name, and `camera` and `camera_format` are refused with `source: "voice_over"`. An unknown camera is refused with a list of every camera connected, and with none connected the answer is "No camera is connected." A camera recording needs the **Camera** permission (**System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Camera**), which is read and never asked for, like the others. The recording starts once the camera has settled at its frame rate (up to a second), and `seconds` counts from its first frame. A camera recording made this way takes the camera from the panel's preview: while it runs, the panel's **Preview** reads "The camera is recording." and the picture comes back when the recording ends. The answer carries `camera` with the camera's `name`, `id` and `format` (for example `1760x1328@30`), plus `problem` when the camera stopped on its own and `note` when it hadn't settled at its rate by the time recording began. The note repeats both. The movie has no sound of its own, so `has_audio` is false. In a new project, the canvas is the file's size at the format's frame rate.
230	
231	With `source: "screen"` (the default) and `camera`, Frame Job records that camera **beside the screen**, at the same time, for a talking head over a screencast. Each stretch of the recording gets a camera movie named after its screen movie, for example `Screen Recording 2026-10-26 at 17.14.33 (Camera).mov`, at the camera's best format or the one `camera_format` names (`camera_format` without `camera` is refused: "With source screen, camera_format needs camera — name the camera to record beside the screen."). The camera files land in the same undo step as the screen's, on one new track named **Camera** in front of everything. Each camera clip starts where its screen clip starts, moved by that stretch's measured `camera_offset`: the camera usually starts a little before the screen, so the clip's first frames are trimmed off rather than the clip starting early, and a camera clip never starts before its screen clip or overlaps the one before it. Each camera clip is laid out in `camera_layout` (`corner_square` by default, the **bottom-right corner**: scaled to fit a box a quarter of the canvas wide and a third of it tall, inside the 90 % guide of **View ▸ Safe Areas**; or `corner_rounded`, `corner_circle`, `side_by_side`, `camera_full`) by one `switch_layout` at its first frame with its stretch's screen clip, as in [A camera beside the screen](#a-camera-beside-the-screen). It's an ordinary clip, so you can move or resize it. With `camera_cutout: true` the camera clips then get Remove Background as their own undo step, **Remove Background**, before any `enhance`, and the answer carries `camera_cutout` (`{clips}`) or `camera_cutout_error` ("No camera clip landed on the timeline, so Remove Background did not run."). Both are refused without `camera` ("With source screen, camera_layout needs camera — name the camera to record beside the screen."), with `source: "voice_over"` and `"camera"`, and with `place: false` ("camera_layout lays out the landed camera clips, so it needs place: true."), all before any permission. The microphone, when asked for, lands on its own track as usual. With `place: false` the camera files are added to the media list only. In a new project, the first screen movie is the document, and its camera (with any microphone) is one undo step named **Add Camera**, or **Add Camera and Microphone**. Each entry of `segments` then also carries `camera_path`, `camera_duration` and `camera_offset` (ticks, positive when the camera began after the screen), `camera_problem` and `camera_note` when something went wrong with that stretch's camera, and `camera_media` and `camera_clip` when known. The camera is looked up, and the Camera permission checked, before the Screen Recording permission. The wait after the recording allows about 105 s more, and 90 s more for each further stretch, because each camera file is read too, and a timeout names the camera files after the movies. The panel's **Record the camera too** box, with a display or a window, makes the same recording, and its **Layout** and Remove the camera's background box are `camera_layout` and `camera_cutout`.
232	
233	**An agent never asks for a permission.** `record_screen` never shows a system prompt, never opens the window picker and never opens System Settings. The Screen Recording permission, and the Microphone permission when one is needed, must already be granted, usually by pressing Record in the panel once. A missing Screen Recording permission is refused with a sentence naming its System Settings pane. A missing Microphone permission is refused with its status (`notDetermined`, `denied` or `restricted`): when it was never answered, the sentence says to press Record in **File ▸ New Recording…** once; otherwise it names the Microphone pane. With `keys: "shortcuts"`, a missing Input Monitoring permission is refused with "Input Monitoring is not granted to Frame Job. Turn it on in System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Input Monitoring." The order is the caller's own mistakes first (`keys` outside `off` and `shortcuts` among them, read after `include_framejob_windows`, then `cursor` outside `separate` and `in_picture`), then the Microphone permission, then Input Monitoring, then `project`, then the Camera and Screen Recording permissions. When Frame Job was launched from a shell, each refusal also names the launching process (its pid) and says to relaunch with `open -a "Frame Job"` or grant the terminal.
234	
235	Refusals come in a fixed order. The caller's own argument mistakes come first, so they're answered even without any permission: `seconds` missing or out of range, then `source` and the arguments that source refuses (`camera` and `camera_format` included), `display` with `window`, an unknown `rate` or `size`, an unknown `keys` or `cursor`, `enhance` without a microphone or with `place: false`, `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays` or `speed_up_typing` with `place: false` and the last two without `keys: "shortcuts"`, `microphone` without the Microphone permission, and a `project` that names nothing open. A camera recording, or a screen recording with `camera`, then looks up the camera, then its `camera_format`, then checks the Camera permission. A screen recording then checks the Screen Recording permission, and only then looks up the display or window. When the screen is locked or every display is asleep, the refusal says so: "No display is shareable right now — the console is locked or every display is asleep; nothing can be recorded until one is."
236	
237	While an agent records, the same menu-bar item appears, so a person at the Mac can pause, resume or stop it. A person's Stop from the menu-bar item or the File menu ends the call early and the recording still lands, with `stopped_by: stopped` and a `duration` shorter than `seconds`. Starting a second recording while one runs is refused with "A recording is already in progress." Pausing shortens what the call records, because `seconds` is wall-clock time.
238	
239	The answer includes `path` (the first file), `duration` (the total recorded), `segments` (one entry per stretch), `pauses` (how many times Pause was pressed), `stopped_by` (`stopped`, `user_stopped` for macOS's own indicator only, or `system_stopped` when a display slept or a camera stopped on its own), `landed` (`document` or `new_project`), the new media and clip ids, `mic_offset`, `mic_problem` and `unreadable` when relevant, and a `note`. See [MCP](mcp.md) for the full tool reference.
240	
241	With `enhance: true`, the call lands the recording as usual and then waits, up to 5 minutes, for the microphone's sound to be analysed, then runs `enhance_voice`'s own steps on the microphone's clips at −16 LUFS (an agent's target never comes from the Normalize row; call `enhance_voice {target_lufs}` afterwards for another). It's its own undo step, **Enhance Voice**, as in [Enhancing the microphone](#enhancing-the-microphone). The answer then also carries `enhance`, the answer `enhance_voice` gives, or `enhance_error`, a sentence saying why it didn't run: nothing measurable (`Nothing could be enhanced. …`), no microphone clip on the timeline, or not analysed within 5 minutes. `project` is read after it. `enhance` is checked right after `place`, before any permission: `enhance: true` without a microphone is refused with "enhance: true enhances the microphone's clip, so it needs microphone: true (or source voice_over).", and with `place: false` with "enhance: true needs place: true — with place: false the microphone lands as media with no clip to enhance."
242	
243	With `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays` or `speed_up_typing`, the call then runs `auto_zoom`, `add_shortcut_overlays` and `speed_up_typing`, in that order, on the recording's screen clips, each as its own undo step as in [When it lands](#when-it-lands). An agent's runs use those tools' defaults (Zoom ×2, Lead 0.6 s, Stay 2.5 s, Follow on, Motion blur 50 %; bottom and dark overlays; ×4 for stretches of 3 s or more, Keep pitch on), never the sheets' remembered values, and `speed_up_typing` waits up to 5 minutes for the speech. The answer then also carries each one's own answer under its name, or a sentence under `auto_zoom_error`, `shortcut_overlays_error` or `speed_up_typing_error`: no screen clip with a cursor file landed, the project busy (or the speech not detected) within 5 minutes, the call stopped first, or the tool's own refusal, which an agent is told rather than asked (a speed-up that leaves a clip silent above ×12 applies and says so in `audio_note`). `project` is read after them. They're checked right after `enhance`, before any permission, in that order: `place: false` is refused first ("auto_zoom: true plans on the landed screen clips, so it needs place: true."), then `shortcut_overlays` and `speed_up_typing` without `keys: "shortcuts"` ("speed_up_typing: true needs keys: \"shortcuts\" — without it the cursor file records no typing to speed up.").
244	
245	*Agents:* `record_screen` (`seconds`, plus the options above). There is no MCP tool for pause or resume. Those are a person's actions.
246	
247	## Limits
248	
249	- The panel records displays, single windows, a camera on its own, and a camera beside a display or a window. A camera records at one of its formats at that format's highest frame rate (not at a lower rate within the format's range). The panel lays a camera beside the screen out in one of five layouts, a corner always the bottom-right one; it has no control for another corner, Stacked, Screen Only, scale or inset. The layout's crop centres on the camera's picture, not on the person. There's no keystroke or callout overlay.
250	- When a stretch of a screen recording is left out because its movie can't be read, its camera file stays on disk and is named with its other kept files, but it isn't added to the project. Only that stretch's microphone is.
251	- There's no global shortcut to stop. Use the menu-bar item or the File menu.
252	- While a screen recording runs, the menu-bar item is the only place to pause or resume besides the File menu. If macOS hides the item, for example behind the notch or in a crowded menu bar, **File ▸ Stop Recording** and **File ▸ Pause Recording** still work.
253	- A recording longer than 9:59:59 shows a label wider than the item was sized for.
254	- When a project is already at its track limit, a recording that needs a new track can't be added. The files stay on disk and the note names them.
255	- If the screen is locked or every display is asleep, no display can be shared, so nothing can be recorded until one wakes.
256	- Record shortcuts writes nothing while any app holds secure input, and a typing mark is a time alone: there's no mode that records what you type.
257	- A **Separate** stretch whose cursor file couldn't be written (the screen never reported its start, or the file couldn't be saved) has no pointer at all: it isn't in the movie and there's nothing to draw it from. The landing's note says so, ending "The pointer is not in the movie either: it was recorded Separate."

151	    ///
152	    /// **One list, one limit.** The pictures and the microphones are ONE
153	    /// grouped edit, so a microphone pair the core refuses takes every
154	    /// picture down with it. The case that reaches it: a document at
155	    /// `MAX_TRACKS` with an empty front track takes the pictures alone (no
156	    /// track is added) and lands NOTHING once a microphone needs its own
157	    /// track. Kept on purpose — half a recording landed, with the voice
158	    /// missing and no undo step that says so, is worse than a refusal — and
159	    /// both doors name the FILES in the refusal, which are on disk whatever
160	    /// happened after them. What is NOT a refusal is a file the core cannot
161	    /// make a clip of at all: it lands as media, with a sentence in `notes`.
162	    static func placement(
163	        _ result: RecordingResult, in document: ProjectDocument, place: Bool
164	    ) throws -> Placement {
165	        assert(Thread.isMainThread)
166	        guard !document.isLiveEditing else {
167	            throw ReelCoreError(
168	                message: "A drag is in progress; the recording can be added when it ends.")
169	        }
170	        if result.isVoiceOver { return try voiceOverPlacement(result, in: document, place: place) }
171	        let scope = document.scope
172	        var trial = document.project
173	        var ops: [ReelOp] = []
174	        var notes: [String] = []
175	
176	        var mediaIds: [UInt32] = []
177	        for segment in result.segments {
178	            mediaIds.append(try addMedia(segment.descriptor, to: &trial, ops: &ops))
179	        }
180	        var pictures: [Landed] = []
181	        if place {
182	            let stretches = try pictureStretches(
183	                of: result, mediaIds: mediaIds, in: trial, scope: scope)
184	            pictures = try addSequence(
185	                stretches, from: document.playhead, scope: scope, to: &trial, ops: &ops,
186	                notes: &notes)
187	            try addRipples(
188	                pictures.compactMap { $0.clip?.id }, of: result, scope: scope, to: &trial,
189	                ops: &ops)
190	        }
191	        let cameras = try addCameras(
192	            result, screenStarts: place ? segmentStarts(pictures.map { $0.at }, of: result) : nil,
193	            screenClips: split(pictures.map { $0.clip?.id }, of: result).segments,
194	            scope: scope, to: &trial, ops: &ops, notes: &notes)
195	        let microphones = try addMicrophones(
196	            voices(of: result), pictureStarts: place ? pictures.map { $0.at } : nil,
197	            scope: scope, to: &trial, ops: &ops, notes: &notes)
198	        let micMedia = split(microphones.media, of: result)
199	        let micClips = split(microphones.clips, of: result)
200	        return Placement(
201	            ops: ops, mediaIds: mediaIds,
202	            clipIds: place
203	                ? split(pictures.map { $0.clip?.id }, of: result).segments
204	                : mediaIds.map { _ in nil },
205	            micMediaIds: micMedia.segments, micClipIds: micClips.segments, notes: notes,
206	            leftOutMicMediaIds: micMedia.leftOut, leftOutMicClipIds: micClips.leftOut,
207	            cameraMediaIds: cameras.media, cameraClipIds: cameras.clips)
208	    }

210	    // MARK: - The steps, each applied purely and read back
211	
212	    /// `add_media` applied purely; the id it minted, read off the result. A
213	    /// path already in the list is the documented IDENTITY
214	    /// (`core/src/edit_track.rs`), not a failure, and then the id is the
215	    /// entry's, matched by the TRIMMED path because that is what the core
216	    /// stored — `backgroundMedia(for:in:)`'s rule. The op stays in the list
217	    /// either way: `applying(_ ops:)` runs every later op after an identity,
218	    /// so one shape serves both cases and the undo step is one.
219	    static func addMedia(
220	        _ descriptor: MediaDescriptor, to trial: inout ReelProject, ops: inout [ReelOp]
221	    ) throws -> UInt32 {
222	        let op = ReelOp.addMedia(descriptor: descriptor)
223	        ops.append(op)
224	        if let added = try trial.applying(op).project {
225	            trial = added
226	            guard let id = added.snapshot.media.last?.id else {
227	                throw ReelCoreError(message: "\(descriptor.path) was added and is not listed.")
228	            }
229	            return id
230	        }
231	        let path = trimmed(descriptor.path)
232	        guard let id = trial.snapshot.media.first(where: { $0.path == path })?.id else {
233	            throw ReelCoreError(message: "\(path) could not be added to the media list.")
234	        }
235	        return id
236	    }

238	    /// The two-try track rule over a SEQUENCE, for a `trial` that holds
239	    /// every `media`: all of them back to back on the front track of the
240	    /// open container, from `at`; if any one REFUSES there — the overlap
241	    /// rule is the only reason the core has — ALL of them on a new track in
242	    /// front of everything, from the same `at`. The sequence never splits: a
243	    /// recording whose first segment sits on one track and whose second on
244	    /// another would read as two recordings, so a refusal part-way discards
245	    /// the front track's half-placed trial whole (it was a copy) and starts
246	    /// the new track's from the trial that holds the media and no clip. The
247	    /// new track's id is `next_id` off the trial, and each clip's is
248	    /// `next_id` off the trial before its own `add_clip`.
249	    ///
250	    /// Only a REFUSAL (nil) falls through to the new track. An `Err` from
251	    /// the first attempt propagates: the caps are the same on either track,
252	    /// so a `try?` here — R1's shape — turned "too many clips" on a full
253	    /// document into a second attempt that added a track and then reported
254	    /// "too many tracks", the wrong cap, when the document was at both.
255	    /// `notes` takes the winning attempt's sentences (the same either way —
256	    /// a picture too short for a frame is too short on any track). The
257	    /// sequence is the whole stretch list, a left-out voice's gap included,
258	    /// so the rule sees every picture where it will land.
259	    private static func addSequence(
260	        _ stretches: [PictureStretch], from at: Ticks, scope: UInt32?,
261	        to trial: inout ReelProject, ops: inout [ReelOp], notes: inout [String]
262	    ) throws -> [Landed] {
263	        let container = try view(of: trial, scope: scope).snapshot
264	        if let front = container.tracks.last?.id {
265	            var attempt = trial
266	            var attemptOps: [ReelOp] = []
267	            var attemptNotes: [String] = []
268	            if let placed = try placeBackToBack(
269	                stretches, on: front, from: at, scope: scope, to: &attempt, ops: &attemptOps,
270	                notes: &attemptNotes)
271	            {
272	                trial = attempt
273	                ops += attemptOps
274	                notes += attemptNotes
275	                return placed
276	            }
277	        }
278	        // Index 0 is the BACK of the stack (§6), so the count is the front.
279	        let addTrack = ReelOp.addTrack(index: container.tracks.count)
280	        let track = trial.snapshot.nextId
281	        guard let withTrack = try trial.applying(addTrack.scoped(scope)).project else {
282	            throw ReelCoreError(message: "A track for the recording could not be added.")
283	        }
284	        var attempt = withTrack
285	        var attemptOps: [ReelOp] = [addTrack]
286	        var attemptNotes: [String] = []
287	        guard
288	            let placed = try placeBackToBack(
289	                stretches, on: track, from: at, scope: scope, to: &attempt, ops: &attemptOps,
290	                notes: &attemptNotes)
291	        else {
292	            throw ReelCoreError(message: "The recording could not be placed on a new track.")
293	        }
294	        trial = attempt
295	        ops += attemptOps
296	        notes += attemptNotes
297	        return placed
298	    }

300	    /// The clip `id` as the core reports it, read off the CONTAINER the ops
301	    /// are measured against — the nest's view while a scope is open, since
302	    /// a nested clip is not in the parent's `clips`. An id the trial does
303	    /// not list after its own `add_clip` accepted it is a throw, not a
304	    /// guess.
305	    static func clip(_ id: UInt32, in trial: ReelProject, scope: UInt32?) throws -> ClipSnapshot {
306	        let container = try view(of: trial, scope: scope).snapshot
307	        guard let clip = container.clips.first(where: { $0.id == id }) else {
308	            throw ReelCoreError(message: "Clip \(id) was placed and is not listed.")
309	        }
310	        return clip
311	    }
312	
313	    /// The container the clip ops are measured against: the nest's view
314	    /// while a scope is open (its tracks and clips at the top level, its
315	    /// `next_id` the parent's), else the trial itself. A scope naming a nest
316	    /// the trial has not got is a refusal, not a fallback — `clampViewState`
317	    /// clears one before anything reads it, so this arm is a race with an
318	    /// undo and the caller should not land on the timeline by accident.
319	    static func view(of trial: ReelProject, scope: UInt32?) throws -> ReelProject {
320	        guard let nest = scope else { return trial }
321	        guard let view = trial.scoped(nest) else {
322	            throw ReelCoreError(message: "The open nest (id \(nest)) is no longer in the project.")
323	        }
324	        return view
325	    }

327	    static func trimmed(_ path: String) -> String {
328	        path.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
329	    }
330	}

351	    /// The undo step's name for `ProjectDocument.untitled(around:)`'s
352	    /// remainder edit when the remainder is a microphone ALONE — one segment
353	    /// with a voice. There the picture is the document — undoing the step
354	    /// removes the voice and keeps the picture — so a step called "Add
355	    /// Recording" would promise to take back what it cannot, and the Edit
356	    /// menu would read "Undo Add Recording" over a project the undo leaves
357	    /// with the recording in it. The `.document` landing keeps `actionName`:
358	    /// its one step really does add and remove both.
359	    static let microphoneActionName = "Add Microphone"
360	
361	    /// The same step's name when the remainder holds more than a voice — a
362	    /// paused recording's later segments, with or without microphones.
363	    /// "Segments" and not "Recording" for the reason above: the FIRST
364	    /// segment is the document and stays under the undo; what the step takes
365	    /// back is the rest.
366	    static let segmentsActionName = "Add Recording Segments"
367	
368	    /// The same step's name for ONE segment whose remainder is its camera
369	    /// beside the screen (spec §11 CAM-10 (4)): the picture is the
370	    /// document, and the step takes the camera back.
371	    static let cameraActionName = "Add Camera"
372	
373	    /// …and for ONE segment whose remainder is its camera and a voice.
374	    static let cameraMicrophoneActionName = "Add Camera and Microphone"
375	
376	    /// Which name `untitled(around:)`'s remainder edit takes. For ONE
377	    /// segment: with a camera beside the screen, "Add Camera and
378	    /// Microphone" when there is any voice and "Add Camera" when there is
379	    /// not (CAM-10 (4)); without one, "Add Microphone" for any voice — its
380	    /// own (R1's landing, R1's name) or a left-out segment's. With neither,
381	    /// the remainder can only be its ripples (CU-31 (c)): "Cursor Clicks".
382	    /// "Add Recording Segments" otherwise. A one-segment recording with no
383	    /// voice, no camera and no ripples has no remainder and no step, and the
384	    /// answer for it is never read.
385	    static func remainderActionName(for result: RecordingResult) -> String {
386	        if result.segments.count == 1 {
387	            let voice =
388	                result.segments[0].micDescriptor != nil
389	                || result.unreadable.contains(where: { $0.micDescriptor != nil })
390	            if result.segments[0].cameraDescriptor != nil {
391	                return voice ? cameraMicrophoneActionName : cameraActionName
392	            }
393	            if voice { return microphoneActionName }
394	            return ripplesActionName

396	        return segmentsActionName

399	    /// Everything a fresh untitled document does NOT already hold, for
400	    /// `ProjectDocument.untitled(around:)`, whose `makeProject` placed the
401	    /// FIRST segment's picture at 0 on track 1 before anything else could
402	    /// run: segments 2…n's media and their pictures on that same track from
403	    /// clip 1's end, then every segment's microphone by the floor rule. nil
404	    /// when there is nothing to add — one segment, no microphone, no camera
405	    /// and no ripples (`wantsRipples` with a cursor not in the picture, CU-31).
406	    /// `placement(_:in:place:)` cannot serve it — the first picture's
407	    /// `add_media` would be the documented identity and its `add_clip` at 0
408	    /// would meet its own clip on the front track, refuse, and put the whole
409	    /// sequence a SECOND time on a new track. The answer reads as a whole
410	    /// landing: `mediaIds[0]` and `clipIds[0]` name the picture the document
411	    /// holds.
412	    ///
413	    /// Clip 1 is the FIRST clip whose source is the first segment's media,
414	    /// and the later pictures go on ITS track from ITS end — read off the
415	    /// document, not assumed to be track 1 at 0. That is exact for the one
416	    /// caller: `makeProject` places exactly one clip. A document holding the
417	    /// same media in several clips has no single answer here, and this
418	    /// method does not pretend to one — it is `untitled(around:)`'s, not a
419	    /// general "add the rest of a recording to a document" op. The later
420	    /// pictures take no two-try rule: a refusal on a fresh document's one
421	    /// track is not a track choice to fall back from but something wrong
422	    /// with a file, and is thrown by name.
423	    ///
424	    /// **Without clip 1** — `makeProject` tolerates a first picture the core
425	    /// refuses (a media with no duration) and opens the file in the Media
426	    /// tab — nothing on the timeline says where the recording is, so the
427	    /// remainder lands as MEDIA ONLY, `place: false`'s shape, with a
428	    /// sentence per file in `notes`. The first shape here placed every
429	    /// voice against a picture at 0, R1's one-segment fallback, which with
430	    /// several voices stacked each one under the last (the floor rule
431	    /// trimming a whole voice off) — a wrong sound where a Media-tab list
432	    /// is at least an honest one.
433	    ///
434	    /// **A left-out segment's readable voice** (#181 item 2) is a stretch:
435	    /// after clip 1 a gap the later pictures skip and a voice at its start;
436	    /// BEFORE clip 1, which is the document at 0, media only with
437	    /// `leadingVoiceNote`; without clip 1, media only with `unplacedNote`.
438	    ///
439	    /// **A camera beside the screen** (spec §11 CAM-10 (4)) lands after the
440	    /// later pictures and before the voices, by `addCameras` against each
441	    /// segment's picture start — clip 1's included — on ONE new track in
442	    /// front of the pictures', laid out with its segment's picture; without
443	    /// clip 1, as media only with
444	    /// `unplacedNote`.
445	    ///
446	    /// **The ripples** (CU-31 (c)) go on clip 1 and the later pictures right
447	    /// after those are placed (`addRipples`); without clip 1 there are none.
448	    static func remainderPlacement(
449	        _ result: RecordingResult, in document: ProjectDocument
450	    ) throws -> Placement? {
451	        assert(Thread.isMainThread)
452	        let hasMicrophone = result.segments.contains { $0.micDescriptor != nil }
453	        let hasLeftOutVoice = result.unreadable.contains { $0.micDescriptor != nil }
454	        let hasCamera = result.segments.contains { $0.cameraDescriptor != nil }
455	        let more = result.segments.count > 1 || hasMicrophone || hasLeftOutVoice || hasCamera
456	        guard more || wantsRipples(result) else { return nil }
457	        let path = trimmed(result.descriptor.path)
458	        let snapshot = document.editedProject.snapshot
459	        guard let mediaId = snapshot.media.first(where: { $0.path == path })?.id else {
460	            throw ReelCoreError(message: "\(path) is not in the document's media list.")
461	        }
462	        let first = snapshot.clips.first { clip in
463	            if case .media(let id, _, _) = clip.source { return id == mediaId }
464	            return false
465	        }
466	        let scope = document.scope
467	        var trial = document.project
468	        var ops: [ReelOp] = []
469	        var notes: [String] = []
470	        var mediaIds = [mediaId]
471	        for segment in result.segments.dropFirst() {
472	            mediaIds.append(try addMedia(segment.descriptor, to: &trial, ops: &ops))
473	        }
474	        var starts: [Ticks?]?
475	        var clips: [UInt32?] = result.stretches.map { _ in nil }
476	        if let first = first {
477	            let placed = try remainderStretches(
478	                result, after: first, mediaIds: mediaIds, firstPath: path, scope: scope,
479	                to: &trial, ops: &ops, notes: &notes)
480	            starts = placed.starts
481	            clips = placed.clips
482	            try addRipples(
483	                clips.compactMap { $0 }, of: result, scope: scope, to: &trial, ops: &ops)
484	        } else {
485	            for segment in result.segments.dropFirst() {
486	                notes.append(unplacedNote(segment.descriptor.path, behind: path))
487	            }
488	            for segment in result.segments {
489	                if let camera = segment.cameraDescriptor {
490	                    notes.append(unplacedNote(camera.path, behind: path))
491	                }
492	            }
493	            for segment in result.segments {
494	                if let mic = segment.micDescriptor { notes.append(unplacedNote(mic.path, behind: path)) }
495	            }
496	            for left in result.unreadable {
497	                if let mic = left.micDescriptor { notes.append(unplacedNote(mic.path, behind: path)) }
498	            }
499	        }
500	        let cameras = try addCameras(
501	            result, screenStarts: starts.map { segmentStarts($0, of: result) },
502	            screenClips: split(clips, of: result).segments, scope: scope,
503	            to: &trial, ops: &ops, notes: &notes)
504	        let microphones = try addMicrophones(
505	            voices(of: result), pictureStarts: starts,
506	            scope: scope, to: &trial, ops: &ops, notes: &notes)
507	        // Let in by the ripples alone, and no clip took one: nothing to add.
508	        guard more || !ops.isEmpty else { return nil }
509	        let micMedia = split(microphones.media, of: result)
510	        let micClips = split(microphones.clips, of: result)
511	        return Placement(
512	            ops: ops, mediaIds: mediaIds, clipIds: split(clips, of: result).segments,
513	            micMediaIds: micMedia.segments, micClipIds: micClips.segments, notes: notes,
514	            leftOutMicMediaIds: micMedia.leftOut, leftOutMicClipIds: micClips.leftOut,
515	            cameraMediaIds: cameras.media, cameraClipIds: cameras.clips)
516	    }

531	// "ripple"}}` over the placed screen clips whose media's cursor file is not in
532	// the picture, inside the landing's one step. `placement` calls it right after
533	// `addSequence`, and `remainderPlacement` after the later pictures, with clip

539	extension RecordingLanding {
540	    /// The undo step's name for `untitled(around:)`'s remainder when the
541	    /// ripples are all it holds — the Cursor section's Clicks row's name.
542	    static let ripplesActionName = "Cursor Clicks"
543	
544	    /// Whether the landing writes ripples: Show Clicks was on, the cursor was
545	    /// recorded Separate, and the recording has a picture.
546	    static func wantsRipples(_ result: RecordingResult) -> Bool {
547	        result.choice.showClicks && result.choice.effectiveCursor == .separate
548	            && !result.isVoiceOver
549	    }

551	    /// When `wantsRipples`, one `set_video` over those of `clips` whose media
552	    /// in `trial` has a cursor file not in the picture, applied to `trial` and
553	    /// appended to `ops`; nothing when none qualifies (a segment whose cursor
554	    /// file was not written has no cursor to ripple). A refusal adds nothing:
555	    /// the ripples never take the recording down with them.
556	    static func addRipples(
557	        _ clips: [UInt32], of result: RecordingResult, scope: UInt32?,
558	        to trial: inout ReelProject, ops: inout [ReelOp]
559	    ) throws {
560	        guard wantsRipples(result), !clips.isEmpty else { return }
561	        let media = trial.snapshot.media
562	        var rippled: [UInt32] = []
563	        for id in clips {
564	            let placed = try clip(id, in: trial, scope: scope)
565	            guard case .media(let source, _, _) = placed.source,
566	                let cursor = media.first(where: { $0.id == source })?.cursor,
567	                !cursor.inPicture
568	            else { continue }
569	            rippled.append(id)
570	        }
571	        guard !rippled.isEmpty else { return }
572	        let op = ReelOp.setVideo(
573	            clips: rippled, patch: VideoPatch(cursorPart: CursorPatch(clicks: .ripple)))
574	        guard let next = try trial.applying(op.scoped(scope)).project else { return }
575	        trial = next
576	        ops.append(op)
577	    }

581	/// The recorder panel from the recording's END to the note that says where
582	/// it went (road map 3, R1c) — `RecorderPanelController.swift`'s fourth
583	/// file, cut out of `+Recording.swift` along the line `recordingEnded`
584	/// draws when the R1 review's fixes took that file past the 400-line cap:
585	/// everything before the session's `onFinish` fires stays there, everything
586	/// after it is here.
587	///
588	/// **One door for a finished recording.** The session's `onFinish` — called
589	/// exactly once whoever ended the recording: the panel's Stop, the status
590	/// item's, the system indicator's, a display that slept, a failure — arrives
591	/// at `recordingEnded`, which tears the recording chrome down (the tick, the
592	/// status item, and the `hiddenForRecording` flag that made `show()` beep —
593	/// clearing it, and showing NOTHING) and then lands. A DOCUMENT target
594	/// commits the placement through the document's
595	/// own door (`performGroupedEdit`, then `generateCaches`, the selection, and
596	/// the editor told through `viewStateDidChange`); a NEW PROJECT is
597	/// `ProjectDocument.untitled(around:)`, which does everything. A document
598	/// mid-drag is not committed over the gesture's base handle: the landing is
599	/// retried from a half-second timer until the drag ends, bounded at forty
600	/// tries — **20 s, kept** (lane C's flag, closed by reading): a landing that
601	/// waited for ever would hold the file's note back for ever, and the note
602	/// after the bound names the file, which is on disk either way — and on
603	/// either failure the note names the FILE, which is on disk whatever went
604	/// wrong after it. That timer stays in the DEFAULT run-loop mode on
605	/// purpose, unlike the countdown and the tick: a drag runs the loop in
606	/// tracking mode, so the retry fires when the drag ENDS, which is the
607	/// moment it is for.
608	///
609	/// **The commit is checked by its handle** (R1 review). `performGroupedEdit`
610	/// answers nothing: a refusal beeps or puts up the core's sentence on the
611	/// document's window and returns, and the panel — which cannot see either
612	/// — used to report "added" over a project with nothing in it. The
613	/// document's `project` handle changes ONLY on success (`applyEdit`'s three
614	/// outcomes), so `land` reads it before the commit and compares after, and
615	/// an unchanged handle is a failed landing with the file's path in the
616	/// note. The trial in `RecordingLanding.placement` sees everything the
617	/// commit will, so the arm is reached only by a race the trial cannot see —
618	/// an edit landing between the two on the same run-loop turn — and it is
619	/// there because the alternative is a note that lies.
620	///
621	/// **The note says six things, in order**, through `landingNote`, a pure
622	/// function so a probe can pin every combination without a landing: how the
623	/// recording ended when it was not this panel's own Stop (`.stopped` is the
624	/// status item's Stop too; `.userStopped` is the SYSTEM's indicator, and the
625	/// sentence names it so, now that Frame Job's own item is a menu-bar item as
626	/// well); that the document the person CHOSE had closed, when the choice
627	/// was a document and the landing opened a new project (R1 review — the
628	/// fallback is exact, and a person who chose "Untitled 2" should not have
629	/// to work out why a new window appeared instead); the segments left out
630	/// because their movie would not probe (`unreadableNote`, #97), each naming
631	/// the files it kept; the microphone's
632	/// problem, when the recording is a `.success` whose `micProblem` is set —
633	/// a success, not an error, so the picture lands first and the sentence
634	/// follows it; a resume the recorder refused (`resumeProblem`, STATE on the
635	/// panel and never text read back off the label — the R2 review's defect:
636	/// each end replaced the label whole, so after a refused resume and a clean
637	/// Stop the note was empty and the reveal showed nothing, the opposite of
638	/// what `+Pause.swift` promised); and the placement's own notes, one per
639	/// file the landing could not place. `failedToLand` names every file
640	/// through `filesClause` and carries the unreadable segments', the
641	/// microphone's and the resume's sentences too.
642	///
643	/// **The panel comes back ONLY with something to say** (decision 7, R2c).
644	/// It ordered out at `recordingDidStart` whatever the source, and each of
645	/// the three ends — `landed`, `failedToLand`, the failure arm of
646	/// `recordingEnded` — finishes with `revealIfNoted()`, AFTER its note is
647	/// set: the panel is ordered front when it was on screen as the recording
648	/// began (`showWhenLanded`) and the note is non-empty, and `showWhenLanded`
649	/// is cleared either way. A clean recording lands in its document or opens
650	/// its project and the panel stays away; ⌥⌘N shows it again. The reveal
651	/// belongs to the END and not to `recordingEnded`, because the deferred
652	/// landing's retries can put twenty seconds between the two, and a panel
653	/// shown with "Adding…" and no note yet is the dialog the user asked to be
654	/// rid of.
655	extension RecorderPanelController {
656	    static let landingRetryInterval: TimeInterval = 0.5
657	    static let landingRetryLimit = 40
658	    static let destinationClosedSentence =
659	        "The document you chose was closed, so the recording opened as a new project."
660	
661	    // MARK: - The end, and the landing
662	
663	    func recordingEnded(_ outcome: Result<RecordingResult, Error>) {
664	        disarmTick()
665	        statusItem?.remove()
666	        statusItem = nil
667	        launched = false
668	        hiddenForRecording = false
669	        switch outcome {
670	        case .failure(let error):
671	            phase = .idle
672	            setNote(
673	                [error.localizedDescription, resumeProblem].compactMap { $0 }
674	                    .joined(separator: " "))
675	            revealIfNoted()
676	        case .success(let result):
677	            phase = .landing
678	            landingAttempts = 0
679	            land(result)
680	        }
681	    }
682	
683	    func land(_ result: RecordingResult) {
684	        switch RecordingLanding.resolve(result.choice.destination) {
685	        case .document(let document):
686	            guard !document.isLiveEditing else {
687	                deferLanding(result)
688	                return
689	            }
690	            do {
691	                let placement = try RecordingLanding.placement(result, in: document, place: true)
692	                let before = document.project
693	                document.performGroupedEdit(RecordingLanding.actionName, placement.ops)
694	                // The handle changes only on success (the type doc).
695	                guard document.project !== before else {
696	                    failedToLand(
697	                        result,
698	                        ReelCoreError(
699	                            message: "the project refused the placement and nothing was added"))
700	                    return
701	                }
702	                document.generateCaches()
703	                // Every segment's clip, microphone clips included (R2b); a
704	                // segment that minted none is a nil entry, and its sentence
705	                // is in `placement.notes`.
706	                document.selection = Set(
707	                    (placement.clipIds + placement.micClipIds + placement.leftOutMicClipIds
708	                        + placement.cameraClipIds)
709	                        .compactMap { $0 })
710	                Self.editor(of: document)?.viewStateDidChange()
711	                landed(result, asNewProject: false, notes: placement.notes)
712	                RecordingCutout.apply(result, in: document)  // CO-81: its own step, first
713	                RecordingEnhance.follow(result, in: document)  // AU-68: after the commit
714	                RecordingPolish.follow(result, in: document)  // CU-100: after it, its own steps
715	            } catch {
716	                failedToLand(result, error)
717	            }
718	        case .newProject:
719	            do {
720	                let (opened, notes) = try ProjectDocument.untitled(around: result)
721	                landed(result, asNewProject: true, notes: notes)
722	                RecordingCutout.apply(result, in: opened)  // CO-81: its own step, first
723	                RecordingEnhance.follow(result, in: opened)  // AU-68: after the commit
724	                RecordingPolish.follow(result, in: opened)  // CU-100: after it, its own steps
725	            } catch {
726	                failedToLand(result, error)
727	            }
728	        }
729	    }
730	
731	    /// A drag is in progress: try again when it has had half a second to
732	    /// end, up to the limit — a landing over the gesture's base handle would
733	    /// be undone by the gesture's own end.
734	    private func deferLanding(_ result: RecordingResult) {
735	        landingAttempts += 1
736	        guard landingAttempts <= Self.landingRetryLimit else {
737	            let waited = Int(Double(Self.landingRetryLimit) * Self.landingRetryInterval)
738	            failedToLand(
739	                result,
740	                ReelCoreError(message: "A drag was still in progress after \(waited) s."))
741	            return
742	        }
743	        landingTimer?.invalidate()
744	        landingTimer = Timer.scheduledTimer(
745	            withTimeInterval: Self.landingRetryInterval, repeats: false
746	        ) { [weak self] _ in
747	            self?.landingTimer = nil
748	            self?.land(result)
749	        }
750	    }
751	
752	    /// Back to idle; the note is `landingNote`'s, over the placement's own
753	    /// notes — the unreadable segments' sentences followed by what became of
754	    /// their readable voices (#181 item 2), said only here, on a landing
755	    /// that succeeded — led by every segment's camera sentences beside the
756	    /// screen (`cameraSegmentsNote`, spec §11 CAM-10 (8)) — and the reveal
757	    /// last.
758	    private func landed(_ result: RecordingResult, asNewProject: Bool, notes placed: [String]) {
759	        phase = .idle
760	        rebuildDestinations()
761	        // Then every segment's cursor problem (spec §11 CU-18).
762	        let notes = [result.cameraSegmentsNote, result.cursorSegmentsNote].compactMap { $0 } + placed
763	        let leftOut = [result.unreadableNote, result.leftOutVoiceNote].compactMap { $0 }
764	        setNote(
765	            Self.landingNote(
766	                stoppedBy: result.stoppedBy, chosen: result.choice.destination,
767	                landedAsNewProject: asNewProject, micProblem: result.micProblem,
768	                resumeProblem: resumeProblem, notes: notes,
769	                unreadable: leftOut.isEmpty ? nil : leftOut.joined(separator: " "),
770	                camera: result.camera, cameraBeside: result.camera != nil && !result.isCamera))
771	        revealIfNoted()
772	    }
773	
774	    /// The files are on disk whatever went wrong after them, so the note
775	    /// names every one (`filesClause`: each segment's movie, and the
776	    /// microphone files that landed) — then what became of an unreadable
777	    /// segment, the microphone, the camera (its `problem` and warm-up `note`,
778	    /// spec §11 CAM-5, then each segment's camera sentences beside the
779	    /// screen, CAM-10 (8)) and a refused resume, when the result or the panel
780	    /// carries those sentences — and the reveal last.
781	    private func failedToLand(_ result: RecordingResult, _ error: any Error) {
782	        phase = .idle
783	        var note =
784	            "The recording was saved at \(result.filesClause) but could not be added: "
785	            + error.localizedDescription
786	        for sentence in [
787	            result.unreadableNote, result.micProblem, result.camera?.problem, result.camera?.note,
788	            result.cameraSegmentsNote, result.cursorSegmentsNote, resumeProblem,
789	        ].compactMap({ $0 })
790	        {
791	            note += " " + sentence
792	        }
793	        setNote(note)
794	        revealIfNoted()
795	    }
796	
797	    /// The panel back on screen after a landing, ONLY when it was on screen
798	    /// as the recording began and the note has something in it (the type
799	    /// doc). Called LAST by each of the three ends, after the note is set —
800	    /// which is the whole point — and reached after the deferred landing's
801	    /// retries as well, since nothing before it clears `showWhenLanded`.
802	    /// Cleared either way, so a later `show()` of the person's own is not
803	    /// mistaken for this one. Internal so a probe can drive both ways.
804	    func revealIfNoted() {
805	        if showWhenLanded, !noteLabel.stringValue.isEmpty { window?.orderFront(nil) }
806	        showWhenLanded = false
807	    }
808	
809	    /// The landing's note (the type doc): the stop's sentence unless the
810	    /// stop was this panel's own; the closed-document sentence when a chosen
811	    /// document was gone by the time the recording ended; the unreadable
812	    /// segments' sentences; the microphone's problem; a refused resume's
813	    /// sentence; then the placement's notes. Empty for the ordinary case, so
814	    /// `setNote` hides the label. The R2 arguments, #97's `unreadable` and
815	    /// CR1c's `camera` are LAST and default, so the probe's R1 rows read as
816	    /// they did. A CAMERA result (spec §11 CAM-5) says its own stop — the
817	    /// camera's `problem`, else that it stopped on its own — in place of the
818	    /// display's, and its warm-up `note` follows the microphone's problem.
819	    /// A camera BESIDE the screen (`cameraBeside`, spec §11 CAM-10 (8)) is
820	    /// not the recording's stop: the display's sentence stays, and the
821	    /// camera's `problem` follows the microphone's problem, before its note.
822	    static func landingNote(
823	        stoppedBy: StopReason, chosen: RecordingDestination, landedAsNewProject: Bool,
824	        micProblem: String?, resumeProblem: String? = nil, notes: [String] = [],
825	        unreadable: String? = nil, camera: RecordingCamera? = nil, cameraBeside: Bool = false
826	    ) -> String {
827	        var sentences: [String] = []
828	        switch stoppedBy {
829	        case .stopped:
830	            break
831	        case .userStopped:
832	            sentences.append(
833	                "Stopped from the system's screen-recording indicator; the recording was added.")
834	        case .systemStopped:
835	            if let camera, !cameraBeside {
836	                sentences.append(
837	                    (camera.problem ?? "The camera stopped on its own.")
838	                        + " What was captured was added.")
839	            } else {
840	                sentences.append(
841	                    "The system stopped the recording (the display slept or went away); "
842	                        + "what was captured was added.")
843	            }
844	        }
845	        if case .document = chosen, landedAsNewProject {
846	            sentences.append(destinationClosedSentence)
847	        }
848	        if let unreadable { sentences.append(unreadable) }
849	        if let micProblem { sentences.append(micProblem) }
850	        if cameraBeside, let problem = camera?.problem { sentences.append(problem) }
851	        if let note = camera?.note { sentences.append(note) }
852	        if let resumeProblem { sentences.append(resumeProblem) }
853	        sentences.append(contentsOf: notes)
854	        return sentences.joined(separator: " ")
855	    }
856	
857	    /// `AgentServer.editor(_:)`'s lookup; nil for a windowless document.
858	    static func editor(of document: ProjectDocument) -> EditorViewController? {
859	        document.windowControllers
860	            .compactMap { $0.contentViewController as? EditorViewController }
861	            .first
862	    }
863	}
