409	    /// sequence a SECOND time on a new track. The answer reads as a whole
410	    /// landing: `mediaIds[0]` and `clipIds[0]` name the picture the document
411	    /// holds.
412	    ///
413	    /// Clip 1 is the FIRST clip whose source is the first segment's media,
414	    /// and the later pictures go on ITS track from ITS end — read off the
415	    /// document, not assumed to be track 1 at 0. That is exact for the one
416	    /// caller: `makeProject` places exactly one clip. A document holding the
417	    /// same media in several clips has no single answer here, and this
418	    /// method does not pretend to one — it is `untitled(around:)`'s, not a
419	    /// general "add the rest of a recording to a document" op. The later
420	    /// pictures take no two-try rule: a refusal on a fresh document's one
421	    /// track is not a track choice to fall back from but something wrong
422	    /// with a file, and is thrown by name.
423	    ///
424	    /// **Without clip 1** — `makeProject` tolerates a first picture the core
425	    /// refuses (a media with no duration) and opens the file in the Media
426	    /// tab — nothing on the timeline says where the recording is, so the
427	    /// remainder lands as MEDIA ONLY, `place: false`'s shape, with a
428	    /// sentence per file in `notes`. The first shape here placed every
429	    /// voice against a picture at 0, R1's one-segment fallback, which with
430	    /// several voices stacked each one under the last (the floor rule
431	    /// trimming a whole voice off) — a wrong sound where a Media-tab list
432	    /// is at least an honest one.
433	    ///
434	    /// **A left-out segment's readable voice** (#181 item 2) is a stretch:
435	    /// after clip 1 a gap the later pictures skip and a voice at its start;
436	    /// BEFORE clip 1, which is the document at 0, media only with
437	    /// `leadingVoiceNote`; without clip 1, media only with `unplacedNote`.
438	    ///
439	    /// **A camera beside the screen** (spec §11 CAM-10 (4)) lands after the
440	    /// later pictures and before the voices, by `addCameras` against each
441	    /// segment's picture start — clip 1's included — on ONE new track in
442	    /// front of the pictures', laid out with its segment's picture; without
443	    /// clip 1, as media only with
444	    /// `unplacedNote`.
445	    ///
446	    /// **The ripples** (CU-31 (c)) go on clip 1 and the later pictures right
447	    /// after those are placed (`addRipples`); without clip 1 there are none.
448	    static func remainderPlacement(
449	        _ result: RecordingResult, in document: ProjectDocument
450	    ) throws -> Placement? {
451	        assert(Thread.isMainThread)
452	        let hasMicrophone = result.segments.contains { $0.micDescriptor != nil }
453	        let hasLeftOutVoice = result.unreadable.contains { $0.micDescriptor != nil }
454	        let hasCamera = result.segments.contains { $0.cameraDescriptor != nil }
455	        let more = result.segments.count > 1 || hasMicrophone || hasLeftOutVoice || hasCamera
456	        guard more || wantsRipples(result) else { return nil }
457	        let path = trimmed(result.descriptor.path)
458	        let snapshot = document.editedProject.snapshot
459	        guard let mediaId = snapshot.media.first(where: { $0.path == path })?.id else {
460	            throw ReelCoreError(message: "\(path) is not in the document's media list.")
461	        }
462	        let first = snapshot.clips.first { clip in
463	            if case .media(let id, _, _) = clip.source { return id == mediaId }
464	            return false
465	        }
466	        let scope = document.scope
467	        var trial = document.project
468	        var ops: [ReelOp] = []
469	        var notes: [String] = []
470	        var mediaIds = [mediaId]
471	        for segment in result.segments.dropFirst() {
472	            mediaIds.append(try addMedia(segment.descriptor, to: &trial, ops: &ops))
473	        }
474	        var starts: [Ticks?]?
475	        var clips: [UInt32?] = result.stretches.map { _ in nil }
476	        if let first = first {
477	            let placed = try remainderStretches(
478	                result, after: first, mediaIds: mediaIds, firstPath: path, scope: scope,
479	                to: &trial, ops: &ops, notes: &notes)
480	            starts = placed.starts
481	            clips = placed.clips
482	            try addRipples(
483	                clips.compactMap { $0 }, of: result, scope: scope, to: &trial, ops: &ops)
484	        } else {
485	            for segment in result.segments.dropFirst() {
486	                notes.append(unplacedNote(segment.descriptor.path, behind: path))
487	            }
488	            for segment in result.segments {
489	                if let camera = segment.cameraDescriptor {
490	                    notes.append(unplacedNote(camera.path, behind: path))
491	                }
492	            }
493	            for segment in result.segments {
494	                if let mic = segment.micDescriptor { notes.append(unplacedNote(mic.path, behind: path)) }
495	            }
496	            for left in result.unreadable {
497	                if let mic = left.micDescriptor { notes.append(unplacedNote(mic.path, behind: path)) }
498	            }
499	        }
500	        let cameras = try addCameras(
501	            result, screenStarts: starts.map { segmentStarts($0, of: result) },
502	            screenClips: split(clips, of: result).segments, scope: scope,
503	            to: &trial, ops: &ops, notes: &notes)
504	        let microphones = try addMicrophones(
505	            voices(of: result), pictureStarts: starts,
506	            scope: scope, to: &trial, ops: &ops, notes: &notes)
507	        // Let in by the ripples alone, and no clip took one: nothing to add.
508	        guard more || !ops.isEmpty else { return nil }
509	        let micMedia = split(microphones.media, of: result)
510	        let micClips = split(microphones.clips, of: result)
511	        return Placement(
512	            ops: ops, mediaIds: mediaIds, clipIds: split(clips, of: result).segments,
513	            micMediaIds: micMedia.segments, micClipIds: micClips.segments, notes: notes,
514	            leftOutMicMediaIds: micMedia.leftOut, leftOutMicClipIds: micClips.leftOut,
515	            cameraMediaIds: cameras.media, cameraClipIds: cameras.clips)
516	    }

551	    /// When `wantsRipples`, one `set_video` over those of `clips` whose media

554	    /// file was not written has no cursor to ripple). A refusal adds nothing:
555	    /// the ripples never take the recording down with them.
556	    static func addRipples(
557	        _ clips: [UInt32], of result: RecordingResult, scope: UInt32?,
558	        to trial: inout ReelProject, ops: inout [ReelOp]
559	    ) throws {

561	        let media = trial.snapshot.media

581	/// The recorder panel from the recording's END to the note that says where
582	/// it went (road map 3, R1c) — `RecorderPanelController.swift`'s fourth
583	/// file, cut out of `+Recording.swift` along the line `recordingEnded`
584	/// draws when the R1 review's fixes took that file past the 400-line cap:
585	/// everything before the session's `onFinish` fires stays there, everything
586	/// after it is here.
587	///
588	/// **One door for a finished recording.** The session's `onFinish` — called
589	/// exactly once whoever ended the recording: the panel's Stop, the status
590	/// item's, the system indicator's, a display that slept, a failure — arrives
591	/// at `recordingEnded`, which tears the recording chrome down (the tick, the
592	/// status item, and the `hiddenForRecording` flag that made `show()` beep —
593	/// clearing it, and showing NOTHING) and then lands. A DOCUMENT target
594	/// commits the placement through the document's
595	/// own door (`performGroupedEdit`, then `generateCaches`, the selection, and
596	/// the editor told through `viewStateDidChange`); a NEW PROJECT is
597	/// `ProjectDocument.untitled(around:)`, which does everything. A document
598	/// mid-drag is not committed over the gesture's base handle: the landing is
599	/// retried from a half-second timer until the drag ends, bounded at forty
600	/// tries — **20 s, kept** (lane C's flag, closed by reading): a landing that
601	/// waited for ever would hold the file's note back for ever, and the note
602	/// after the bound names the file, which is on disk either way — and on
603	/// either failure the note names the FILE, which is on disk whatever went
604	/// wrong after it. That timer stays in the DEFAULT run-loop mode on
605	/// purpose, unlike the countdown and the tick: a drag runs the loop in
606	/// tracking mode, so the retry fires when the drag ENDS, which is the
607	/// moment it is for.
608	///
609	/// **The commit is checked by its handle** (R1 review). `performGroupedEdit`
610	/// answers nothing: a refusal beeps or puts up the core's sentence on the
611	/// document's window and returns, and the panel — which cannot see either
612	/// — used to report "added" over a project with nothing in it. The
613	/// document's `project` handle changes ONLY on success (`applyEdit`'s three
614	/// outcomes), so `land` reads it before the commit and compares after, and
615	/// an unchanged handle is a failed landing with the file's path in the
616	/// note. The trial in `RecordingLanding.placement` sees everything the
617	/// commit will, so the arm is reached only by a race the trial cannot see —
618	/// an edit landing between the two on the same run-loop turn — and it is
619	/// there because the alternative is a note that lies.
620	///
621	/// **The note says six things, in order**, through `landingNote`, a pure
622	/// function so a probe can pin every combination without a landing: how the
623	/// recording ended when it was not this panel's own Stop (`.stopped` is the
624	/// status item's Stop too; `.userStopped` is the SYSTEM's indicator, and the
625	/// sentence names it so, now that Frame Job's own item is a menu-bar item as
626	/// well); that the document the person CHOSE had closed, when the choice
627	/// was a document and the landing opened a new project (R1 review — the
628	/// fallback is exact, and a person who chose "Untitled 2" should not have
629	/// to work out why a new window appeared instead); the segments left out
630	/// because their movie would not probe (`unreadableNote`, #97), each naming
631	/// the files it kept; the microphone's
632	/// problem, when the recording is a `.success` whose `micProblem` is set —
633	/// a success, not an error, so the picture lands first and the sentence
634	/// follows it; a resume the recorder refused (`resumeProblem`, STATE on the
635	/// panel and never text read back off the label — the R2 review's defect:
636	/// each end replaced the label whole, so after a refused resume and a clean
637	/// Stop the note was empty and the reveal showed nothing, the opposite of
638	/// what `+Pause.swift` promised); and the placement's own notes, one per
639	/// file the landing could not place. `failedToLand` names every file
640	/// through `filesClause` and carries the unreadable segments', the
641	/// microphone's and the resume's sentences too.
642	///
643	/// **The panel comes back ONLY with something to say** (decision 7, R2c).
644	/// It ordered out at `recordingDidStart` whatever the source, and each of
645	/// the three ends — `landed`, `failedToLand`, the failure arm of

655	extension RecorderPanelController {
656	    static let landingRetryInterval: TimeInterval = 0.5
657	    static let landingRetryLimit = 40

659	        "The document you chose was closed, so the recording opened as a new project."

661	    // MARK: - The end, and the landing

663	    func recordingEnded(_ outcome: Result<RecordingResult, Error>) {

665	        statusItem?.remove()

667	        launched = false
668	        hiddenForRecording = false

670	        case .failure(let error):
671	            phase = .idle
672	            setNote(
673	                [error.localizedDescription, resumeProblem].compactMap { $0 }
674	                    .joined(separator: " "))
675	            revealIfNoted()
676	        case .success(let result):
677	            phase = .landing
678	            landingAttempts = 0

684	        switch RecordingLanding.resolve(result.choice.destination) {
685	        case .document(let document):
686	            guard !document.isLiveEditing else {
687	                deferLanding(result)

690	            do {
691	                let placement = try RecordingLanding.placement(result, in: document, place: true)

693	                document.performGroupedEdit(RecordingLanding.actionName, placement.ops)

695	                guard document.project !== before else {

698	                        ReelCoreError(
699	                            message: "the project refused the placement and nothing was added"))

703	                // Every segment's clip, microphone clips included (R2b); a
704	                // segment that minted none is a nil entry, and its sentence
705	                // is in `placement.notes`.
706	                document.selection = Set(
707	                    (placement.clipIds + placement.micClipIds + placement.leftOutMicClipIds
708	                        + placement.cameraClipIds)
709	                        .compactMap { $0 })
710	                Self.editor(of: document)?.viewStateDidChange()
711	                landed(result, asNewProject: false, notes: placement.notes)
712	                RecordingCutout.apply(result, in: document)  // CO-81: its own step, first
713	                RecordingEnhance.follow(result, in: document)  // AU-68: after the commit
714	                RecordingPolish.follow(result, in: document)  // CU-100: after it, its own steps
715	            } catch {
716	                failedToLand(result, error)
717	            }
718	        case .newProject:
719	            do {
720	                let (opened, notes) = try ProjectDocument.untitled(around: result)
721	                landed(result, asNewProject: true, notes: notes)
722	                RecordingCutout.apply(result, in: opened)  // CO-81: its own step, first
723	                RecordingEnhance.follow(result, in: opened)  // AU-68: after the commit
724	                RecordingPolish.follow(result, in: opened)  // CU-100: after it, its own steps
725	            } catch {
726	                failedToLand(result, error)
727	            }
728	        }
729	    }
730	
731	    /// A drag is in progress: try again when it has had half a second to
732	    /// end, up to the limit — a landing over the gesture's base handle would
733	    /// be undone by the gesture's own end.
734	    private func deferLanding(_ result: RecordingResult) {
735	        landingAttempts += 1
736	        guard landingAttempts <= Self.landingRetryLimit else {
737	            let waited = Int(Double(Self.landingRetryLimit) * Self.landingRetryInterval)
738	            failedToLand(
739	                result,
740	                ReelCoreError(message: "A drag was still in progress after \(waited) s."))
741	            return
742	        }
743	        landingTimer?.invalidate()
744	        landingTimer = Timer.scheduledTimer(
745	            withTimeInterval: Self.landingRetryInterval, repeats: false
746	        ) { [weak self] _ in
747	            self?.landingTimer = nil
748	            self?.land(result)
749	        }
750	    }
751	
752	    /// Back to idle; the note is `landingNote`'s, over the placement's own
753	    /// notes — the unreadable segments' sentences followed by what became of
754	    /// their readable voices (#181 item 2), said only here, on a landing
755	    /// that succeeded — led by every segment's camera sentences beside the
756	    /// screen (`cameraSegmentsNote`, spec §11 CAM-10 (8)) — and the reveal
757	    /// last.
758	    private func landed(_ result: RecordingResult, asNewProject: Bool, notes placed: [String]) {
759	        phase = .idle
760	        rebuildDestinations()
761	        // Then every segment's cursor problem (spec §11 CU-18).
762	        let notes = [result.cameraSegmentsNote, result.cursorSegmentsNote].compactMap { $0 } + placed
763	        let leftOut = [result.unreadableNote, result.leftOutVoiceNote].compactMap { $0 }
764	        setNote(
765	            Self.landingNote(
766	                stoppedBy: result.stoppedBy, chosen: result.choice.destination,
767	                landedAsNewProject: asNewProject, micProblem: result.micProblem,
768	                resumeProblem: resumeProblem, notes: notes,
769	                unreadable: leftOut.isEmpty ? nil : leftOut.joined(separator: " "),
770	                camera: result.camera, cameraBeside: result.camera != nil && !result.isCamera))
771	        revealIfNoted()
772	    }
773	
774	    /// The files are on disk whatever went wrong after them, so the note
775	    /// names every one (`filesClause`: each segment's movie, and the
776	    /// microphone files that landed) — then what became of an unreadable
777	    /// segment, the microphone, the camera (its `problem` and warm-up `note`,
778	    /// spec §11 CAM-5, then each segment's camera sentences beside the
779	    /// screen, CAM-10 (8)) and a refused resume, when the result or the panel
780	    /// carries those sentences — and the reveal last.
781	    private func failedToLand(_ result: RecordingResult, _ error: any Error) {
782	        phase = .idle
783	        var note =
784	            "The recording was saved at \(result.filesClause) but could not be added: "
785	            + error.localizedDescription
786	        for sentence in [
787	            result.unreadableNote, result.micProblem, result.camera?.problem, result.camera?.note,
788	            result.cameraSegmentsNote, result.cursorSegmentsNote, resumeProblem,
789	        ].compactMap({ $0 })
790	        {
791	            note += " " + sentence
792	        }
793	        setNote(note)
794	        revealIfNoted()
795	    }
796	
797	    /// The panel back on screen after a landing, ONLY when it was on screen
798	    /// as the recording began and the note has something in it (the type
799	    /// doc). Called LAST by each of the three ends, after the note is set —
800	    /// which is the whole point — and reached after the deferred landing's
801	    /// retries as well, since nothing before it clears `showWhenLanded`.
802	    /// Cleared either way, so a later `show()` of the person's own is not
803	    /// mistaken for this one. Internal so a probe can drive both ways.
804	    func revealIfNoted() {
805	        if showWhenLanded, !noteLabel.stringValue.isEmpty { window?.orderFront(nil) }
806	        showWhenLanded = false
807	    }
808	
809	    /// The landing's note (the type doc): the stop's sentence unless the
810	    /// stop was this panel's own; the closed-document sentence when a chosen
811	    /// document was gone by the time the recording ended; the unreadable
812	    /// segments' sentences; the microphone's problem; a refused resume's
813	    /// sentence; then the placement's notes. Empty for the ordinary case, so
814	    /// `setNote` hides the label. The R2 arguments, #97's `unreadable` and
815	    /// CR1c's `camera` are LAST and default, so the probe's R1 rows read as
816	    /// they did. A CAMERA result (spec §11 CAM-5) says its own stop — the
817	    /// camera's `problem`, else that it stopped on its own — in place of the
818	    /// display's, and its warm-up `note` follows the microphone's problem.
819	    /// A camera BESIDE the screen (`cameraBeside`, spec §11 CAM-10 (8)) is
820	    /// not the recording's stop: the display's sentence stays, and the
821	    /// camera's `problem` follows the microphone's problem, before its note.
822	    static func landingNote(
823	        stoppedBy: StopReason, chosen: RecordingDestination, landedAsNewProject: Bool,
824	        micProblem: String?, resumeProblem: String? = nil, notes: [String] = [],
825	        unreadable: String? = nil, camera: RecordingCamera? = nil, cameraBeside: Bool = false
826	    ) -> String {
827	        var sentences: [String] = []
828	        switch stoppedBy {
829	        case .stopped:
830	            break
831	        case .userStopped:
832	            sentences.append(
833	                "Stopped from the system's screen-recording indicator; the recording was added.")
834	        case .systemStopped:
835	            if let camera, !cameraBeside {
836	                sentences.append(
837	                    (camera.problem ?? "The camera stopped on its own.")
838	                        + " What was captured was added.")
839	            } else {
840	                sentences.append(
841	                    "The system stopped the recording (the display slept or went away); "
842	                        + "what was captured was added.")
843	            }
844	        }
845	        if case .document = chosen, landedAsNewProject {
846	            sentences.append(destinationClosedSentence)
847	        }
848	        if let unreadable { sentences.append(unreadable) }
849	        if let micProblem { sentences.append(micProblem) }
850	        if cameraBeside, let problem = camera?.problem { sentences.append(problem) }
851	        if let note = camera?.note { sentences.append(note) }
852	        if let resumeProblem { sentences.append(resumeProblem) }
853	        sentences.append(contentsOf: notes)
854	        return sentences.joined(separator: " ")
855	    }

857	    /// `AgentServer.editor(_:)`'s lookup; nil for a windowless document.
858	    static func editor(of document: ProjectDocument) -> EditorViewController? {
859	        document.windowControllers
860	            .compactMap { $0.contentViewController as? EditorViewController }
861	            .first
862	    }
863	}

3	/// The recorder's polish on landing (road map "creator-jobs" CU10, spec §11 CU-100…CU-102):
4	/// Auto Zoom, Add Shortcut Overlays and Speed Up Typing run over a finished screen recording's
5	/// clips as FOLLOW-UPS to the landing — never part of it (AU-68's shape). The landing commits
6	/// at once and is unchanged; each command follows as its own undo step, named by its title, in
7	/// `allCases` order, after any Enhance Voice: zooms are planned on unsplit clips, and the
8	/// speed-up's stretches avoid the overlays (CU-91).
9	///
10	/// The values and the pure decision are here: which commands a choice asks for (`commands`),
11	/// which files are the screen (`screenPaths`), which clips they are now (`screenClips`,
12	/// recomputed at every check, so the speed-up's splits and clips added later are seen), whether
13	/// a command can run (`isReady`), the sentences, and `decide`. The two doors share them: the
14	/// panel through `follow` (`RecordingPolish+Follow.swift`), and `record_screen` /
15	/// `land_recording`'s tool door through `AgentServer.polishLanded`, which polls `decide` from
16	/// the server thread.
17	enum RecordingPolish {
18	    /// The three commands, in the order they run.
19	    enum Command: String, CaseIterable {
20	        case autoZoom = "auto_zoom"
21	        case shortcutOverlays = "shortcut_overlays"
22	        case speedUpTyping = "speed_up_typing"
23	
24	        /// Each command's undo step, its `actionName`.
25	        var title: String {
26	            switch self {
27	            case .autoZoom: return AutoZoom.actionName
28	            case .shortcutOverlays: return ShortcutOverlays.actionName
29	            case .speedUpTyping: return SpeedUpTyping.actionName
30	            }
31	        }
32	
33	        /// The menu item a person runs it by.
34	        var menuPath: String {
35	            switch self {
36	            case .autoZoom: return "Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…"
37	            case .shortcutOverlays: return "Clip ▸ Add Shortcut Overlays"
38	            case .speedUpTyping: return "Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…"
39	            }
40	        }
41	    }
42	
43	    /// What one check decides (CU-101 (e)).
44	    enum Step: Equatable {
45	        case wait
46	        case run(Command, [UInt32])
47	        case drop
48	        case giveUp(Command)
49	    }
50	
51	    /// One check every half second, the landing's (and Enhance's) own interval.
52	    static let checkInterval: TimeInterval = RecordingEnhance.checkInterval
53	    /// Past this since a command's clock started, it is given up on.
54	    static let waitLimit: TimeInterval = 300
55	
56	    /// The commands `choice` asks for, always in `allCases` order.
57	    static func commands(of choice: RecordingChoice) -> [Command] {
58	        Command.allCases.filter { command in
59	            switch command {
60	            case .autoZoom: return choice.autoZoom
61	            case .shortcutOverlays: return choice.shortcutOverlays
62	            case .speedUpTyping: return choice.speedUpTyping
63	            }
64	        }
65	    }
66	
67	    // MARK: - The screen
68	
69	    /// Each segment's movie, the screen's files; none for a voice-over or a camera alone, whose
70	    /// segments are no screen. Pure; empty paths dropped, each path once.
71	    static func screenPaths(of result: RecordingResult) -> [String] {
72	        guard !result.isVoiceOver, result.choice.source != .camera else { return [] }
73	        var seen: Set<String> = []
74	        return result.segments.map { $0.descriptor.path }.filter {
75	            !$0.isEmpty && seen.insert($0).inserted
76	        }
77	    }
78	
79	    /// Every clip of the open container whose media is one of `paths` AND has a cursor file,
80	    /// in id order. Main.
81	    static func screenClips(_ paths: [String], in document: ProjectDocument) -> [UInt32] {
82	        let wanted = Set(paths)
83	        guard !wanted.isEmpty else { return [] }
84	        let snapshot = document.editedProject.snapshot
85	        return snapshot.clips.filter { clip in
86	            guard let media = snapshot.media(for: clip) else { return false }
87	            return wanted.contains(media.path) && media.cursor != nil
88	        }.map(\.id).sorted()
89	    }
90	
91	    // MARK: - Readiness
92	
93	    /// Documents whose speech wait has started the cache pass, by `recipeKey` (CU-101 (c)).
94	    private static var cachesStarted: Set<Int> = []
95	
96	    /// CU-101 (c). Auto Zoom and Add Shortcut Overlays need only the cursor files, which the
97	    /// caller has read. The speed-up is ready unless `SpeedUpTyping.resolve` answers `.waiting`;
98	    /// its first `.waiting` for the document starts `generateCaches()` (a pass that could not
99	    /// read a file is not retried until the next open). A throw counts as ready, so the run
100	    /// reports the refusal. Main.
101	    static func isReady(
102	        _ command: Command, clips: [UInt32], tracks: [UInt32: ReelCursor],
103	        speedUp: SpeedUpTypingSettings, in document: ProjectDocument
104	    ) -> Bool {
105	        guard command == .speedUpTyping else { return true }
106	        let snapshot = document.editedProject.snapshot
107	        let outcome: SpeedUpTypingOutcome
108	        do {
109	            outcome = try SpeedUpTyping.resolve(
110	                clips.compactMap { snapshot.clip($0) }, tracks: tracks,
111	                project: document.editedProject, cacheDirectory: document.cacheDirectory,
112	                settings: speedUp, from: nil, to: nil)
113	        } catch {
114	            return true
115	        }
116	        guard case .waiting = outcome else {
117	            cachesStarted.remove(document.recipeKey)
118	            return true
119	        }
120	        if cachesStarted.insert(document.recipeKey).inserted { document.generateCaches() }
121	        return false
122	    }
123	
124	    /// The wait for `document` is over: a later wait starts the pass again. Main.
125	    static func forgetWait(_ document: ProjectDocument) {
126	        cachesStarted.remove(document.recipeKey)
127	    }
128	
129	    /// CU-101 (e), in this order. Pure.
130	    static func decide(
131	        command: Command, clips: [UInt32], enhancing: Bool, ready: Bool, busy: Bool,
132	        elapsed: TimeInterval
133	    ) -> Step {
134	        if clips.isEmpty { return .drop }
135	        if enhancing { return .wait }
136	        if ready && !busy { return .run(command, clips) }
137	        if elapsed >= waitLimit { return .giveUp(command) }
138	        return .wait
139	    }
140	
141	    // MARK: - Sentences (CU-101 (k))
142	
143	    static func noScreenSentence(_ c: Command) -> String {
144	        "No screen clip with a cursor file landed on the timeline, so \(c.title) did not run."
145	    }
146	
147	    static func notReadySentence(_ c: Command, tool: Bool) -> String {
148	        let why =
149	            c == .speedUpTyping
150	            ? "its speech was not detected within 5 minutes."
151	            : "the project was busy for 5 minutes."
152	        let way =
153	            tool
154	            ? " Call \(c.rawValue) with its clips."
155	            : " Select its clips and choose \(c.menuPath)."
156	        return "\(c.title) did not run on the recording: " + why + way
157	    }
158	
159	    static func stoppedSentence(_ c: Command) -> String {
160	        "record_screen was stopped before \(c.title) ran, so it did not run."
161	    }
162	
163	    /// The panel box's tooltip (CU-102 (a)), naming the step.
164	    static func tooltip(_ c: Command) -> String {
165	        "After the recording lands, run \(c.menuPath) on its screen clips as its own undo step, "
166	            + "\"\(c.title)\"."
167	    }
168	}

171	/// The recorder panel's polish follow (road map "creator-jobs" CU10, spec §11 CU-101 (f)…(i)):
172	/// a repeating timer per LANDING — never joined with another, unlike Enhance's — in the run
173	/// loop's DEFAULT mode, so a drag (tracking mode) holds it. Each firing decides for the first
174	/// command still to run; the follow ends FIRST, its timer invalidated and its entry removed, on
175	/// `.drop`, on `.giveUp`, before the last run, or when the cursor files fail to read, and then
176	/// the step acts. A refusal from one run moves on to the next command, whose clock starts then.
177	///
178	/// The panel's settings are what each menu door would use (CU-101 (g)): Auto Zoom's remembered
179	/// sheet values with Zoom on typing on whenever the files hold typing, the overlays' defaults
180	/// and Speed Up Typing's remembered sheet values. Nothing here asks: a plan with no ops and a
181	/// `.drop` are quiet, and a refusal, a give-up or a read failure is said at the inspector's foot
182	/// (`projectDocumentDidRefuse`), with no beep and no sheet (CU-101 (h)). A timer is not an
183	/// AppKit event, so every commit is `performGroupedEdit`.
184	extension RecordingPolish {
185	    /// One landing's follow.
186	    private final class Follow {
187	        weak var document: ProjectDocument?
188	        let paths: [String]
189	        let scope: UInt32?
190	        var commands: [Command]
191	        var started = Date()
192	        var enhancing = false
193	        /// The cursor files, by media id, once read; `reading` while a read is out.
194	        var tracks: [UInt32: ReelCursor]?
195	        var reading = false
196	        var timer: Timer?
197	
198	        init(document: ProjectDocument, paths: [String], scope: UInt32?, commands: [Command]) {
199	            self.document = document
200	            self.paths = paths
201	            self.scope = scope
202	            self.commands = commands
203	        }
204	    }
205	
206	    /// The follows under way, by a number minted per landing.
207	    private static var follows: [Int: Follow] = [:]
208	    private static var minted = 0
209	
210	    /// The panel's landing hands its result here once it has committed (after Enhance's
211	    /// follow). A no-op unless the choice asks for a command. Main.
212	    static func follow(_ result: RecordingResult, in document: ProjectDocument) {
213	        let asked = commands(of: result.choice)
214	        guard !asked.isEmpty else { return }
215	        minted += 1
216	        let id = minted
217	        let follow = Follow(
218	            document: document, paths: screenPaths(of: result), scope: document.scope,
219	            commands: asked)
220	        follows[id] = follow
221	        // `scheduledTimer` adds it in the DEFAULT mode: it waits out a drag.
222	        follow.timer = Timer.scheduledTimer(withTimeInterval: checkInterval, repeats: true) {
223	            [weak document] timer in
224	            guard let document else {
225	                timer.invalidate()
226	                follows[id] = nil
227	                return
228	            }
229	            tick(id, document)
230	        }
231	    }
232	
233	    /// True while any follow of `document` runs. Main.
234	    static func isPending(_ document: ProjectDocument) -> Bool {
235	        follows.values.contains { $0.document === document }
236	    }
237	
238	    /// One firing. Main.
239	    private static func tick(_ id: Int, _ document: ProjectDocument) {
240	        guard let follow = follows[id], let command = follow.commands.first else {
241	            return end(id, document)
242	        }
243	        let clips = screenClips(follow.paths, in: document)
244	        // CU-101 (a): the clock restarts when Enhance Voice's follow ends.
245	        let enhancing = RecordingEnhance.isPending(document)
246	        if follow.enhancing && !enhancing { follow.started = Date() }
247	        follow.enhancing = enhancing
248	        let media = mediaIDs(clips, in: document)
249	        if !clips.isEmpty, !follow.reading,
250	            follow.tracks.map({ !media.isSubset(of: Set($0.keys)) }) ?? true
251	        {
252	            read(id, follow, clips, in: document)
253	        }
254	        let window = RecorderPanelController.editor(of: document)?.view.window
255	        let busy =
256	            RecordingEnhance.isBusy(document, scope: follow.scope) || window == nil
257	            || window?.attachedSheet != nil
258	        let ready =
259	            follow.tracks.map { tracks in
260	                media.isSubset(of: Set(tracks.keys))
261	                    && isReady(
262	                        command, clips: clips, tracks: tracks,
263	                        speedUp: SpeedUpTypingSettings.remembered(.standard), in: document)
264	            } ?? false
265	        let step = decide(
266	            command: command, clips: clips, enhancing: enhancing, ready: ready, busy: busy,
267	            elapsed: Date().timeIntervalSince(follow.started))
268	        switch step {
269	        case .wait:
270	            return
271	        case .drop:
272	            end(id, document)
273	        case .giveUp(let given):
274	            end(id, document)
275	            refuse(given, notReadySentence(given, tool: false), in: document)
276	        case .run(let ran, let ids):
277	            follow.commands.removeFirst()
278	            follow.started = Date()
279	            if follow.commands.isEmpty { end(id, document) }
280	            if let reason = run(ran, clips: ids, tracks: follow.tracks ?? [:], in: document) {
281	                refuse(ran, reason, in: document)
282	            }
283	        }
284	    }
285	
286	    /// The media ids of `clips`. Main.
287	    private static func mediaIDs(_ clips: [UInt32], in document: ProjectDocument) -> Set<UInt32> {
288	        let snapshot = document.editedProject.snapshot
289	        return Set(clips.compactMap { snapshot.clip($0).flatMap { snapshot.media(for: $0)?.id } })
290	    }
291	
292	    /// The clips' cursor files read on a global queue, once; a failure ends the follow and is
293	    /// said under the command it was read for. Main.
294	    private static func read(
295	        _ id: Int, _ follow: Follow, _ clips: [UInt32], in document: ProjectDocument
296	    ) {
297	        let snapshot = document.editedProject.snapshot
298	        let files: [UInt32: URL]
299	        do {
300	            files = try AutoZoom.cursorFiles(clips.compactMap { snapshot.clip($0) }, in: snapshot)
301	        } catch {
302	            return failRead(id, follow, error, in: document)
303	        }
304	        follow.reading = true
305	        DispatchQueue.global(qos: .userInitiated).async {
306	            let read = Result { try AutoZoom.readTracks(files) }
307	            DispatchQueue.main.async { [weak document] in
308	                follow.reading = false
309	                guard let document, follows[id] === follow else { return }
310	                switch read {
311	                case .success(let tracks): follow.tracks = tracks
312	                case .failure(let error): failRead(id, follow, error, in: document)
313	                }
314	            }
315	        }
316	    }
317	
318	    private static func failRead(
319	        _ id: Int, _ follow: Follow, _ error: Error, in document: ProjectDocument
320	    ) {
321	        let command = follow.commands.first ?? .autoZoom
322	        end(id, document)
323	        refuse(command, error.localizedDescription, in: document)
324	    }
325	
326	    private static func end(_ id: Int, _ document: ProjectDocument) {
327	        follows[id]?.timer?.invalidate()
328	        follows[id] = nil
329	        forgetWait(document)
330	    }
331	
332	    // MARK: - The three runs
333	
334	    /// Plans `command` over `clips` and commits it as one grouped step; nil when it applied or
335	    /// had nothing to do, else the sentence to say. Main.
336	    private static func run(
337	        _ command: Command, clips ids: [UInt32], tracks: [UInt32: ReelCursor],
338	        in document: ProjectDocument
339	    ) -> String? {
340	        let snapshot = document.editedProject.snapshot
341	        let clips = ids.compactMap { snapshot.clip($0) }
342	        do {
343	            switch command {
344	            case .autoZoom:
345	                var settings = AutoZoomSettings.remembered(.standard)
346	                settings.typing = AutoZoom.hasTyping(tracks)
347	                let plan = try AutoZoom.plan(
348	                    clips, tracks: tracks, project: document.editedProject, settings: settings,
349	                    from: nil, to: nil)
350	                guard !plan.ops.isEmpty else { return nil }
351	                document.performGroupedEdit(AutoZoom.actionName, plan.ops)
352	            case .shortcutOverlays:
353	                let planned = try ShortcutOverlays.prepared(
354	                    document, clips: ids, tracks: tracks, settings: ShortcutOverlaySettings(),
355	                    from: nil, to: nil)
356	                guard !planned.plan.ops.isEmpty else { return nil }
357	                document.performGroupedEdit(ShortcutOverlays.actionName, planned.plan.ops)
358	            case .speedUpTyping:
359	                return try speedUp(clips, tracks: tracks, in: document)
360	            }
361	        } catch {
362	            return error.localizedDescription
363	        }
364	        return nil
365	    }
366	
367	    /// CU-101 (i): the panel cannot ask Set Speed, so a speed-up that would leave a clip's audio
368	    /// out is not applied and its note is the refusal; otherwise one grouped step, the captions
369	    /// it re-times riding in it.
370	    private static func speedUp(
371	        _ clips: [ClipSnapshot], tracks: [UInt32: ReelCursor], in document: ProjectDocument
372	    ) throws -> String? {
373	        let outcome = try SpeedUpTyping.resolve(
374	            clips, tracks: tracks, project: document.editedProject,
375	            cacheDirectory: document.cacheDirectory,
376	            settings: SpeedUpTypingSettings.remembered(.standard), from: nil, to: nil)
377	        guard case .planned(let speechOps, let plan) = outcome else {
378	            return notReadySentence(.speedUpTyping, tool: false)
379	        }
380	        guard !plan.ops.isEmpty else { return nil }
381	        let step = CaptionRetime.withRetime(
382	            SpeedUpTyping.actionName, speechOps + plan.ops, on: document.editedProject)
383	        let crossing =
384	            SpeedAudioDrop.mayCross(step.ops)
385	            ? SpeedAudioDrop.crossing(applying: step.ops, to: document.editedProject) : []

155	/// Decision 2 (road map 3 §0): a recording is ORIGINAL footage and lives in
156	/// `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/`, named by date and time — never in the
157	/// package (an untitled document has none) and never in the temporary
158	/// directory (where a cache is regenerable and footage would be lost). The
159	/// folder is created on demand, and `-RCRecordingFolder` overrides it the
160	/// way `-RCFFmpegPath` overrides the binary (`FFmpegRewrap.locate`), so a
161	/// proof can record into `tools/proof/work/` and delete it.
162	enum RecordingFiles {
163	    /// The launch-argument override, read from `UserDefaults.standard` so it
164	    /// works from the argument domain (`-RCRecordingFolder ~/x` on the
165	    /// command line, or a pinned volatile domain in a probe).
166	    static let folderDefaultsKey = "RCRecordingFolder"
167	
168	    /// The default folder's name under `~/Movies`.
169	    static let folderName = "Frame Job Recordings"
170	
171	    /// The folder a recording goes into: the override, tilde-expanded, when
172	    /// one is set; `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/` otherwise. Nothing is
173	    /// created here — `create(_:)` is called at the moment a recording has
174	    /// something to put in it, `AppSupport`'s rule.
175	    static func folder() -> URL {
176	        if let override = UserDefaults.standard.string(forKey: folderDefaultsKey),
177	            !override.isEmpty
178	        {
179	            return URL(
180	                fileURLWithPath: (override as NSString).expandingTildeInPath, isDirectory: true)
181	        }
182	        let movies =
183	            FileManager.default.urls(for: .moviesDirectory, in: .userDomainMask).first
184	            ?? FileManager.default.homeDirectoryForCurrentUser.appendingPathComponent(
185	                "Movies", isDirectory: true)
186	        return movies.appendingPathComponent(folderName, isDirectory: true)
187	    }
188	
189	    /// `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22` — the Screenshot app's
190	    /// spelling, in the machine's own time zone. The formatter is pinned to
191	    /// `en_US_POSIX` so a locale with another digit set or a 12-hour clock
192	    /// cannot change the name's shape; the seconds make a name unique across
193	    /// the app's own recordings and `uniqueURL` handles the rest.
194	    static func stem(at date: Date) -> String {
195	        let formatter = DateFormatter()
196	        formatter.locale = Locale(identifier: "en_US_POSIX")
197	        formatter.timeZone = .current
198	        formatter.dateFormat = "'Screen Recording' yyyy-MM-dd 'at' HH.mm.ss"
199	        return formatter.string(from: date)
200	    }
201	
202	    /// `Voice-over 2026-10-02 at 09.15.04` — a voice-over's file, `stem(at:)`'s
203	    /// spelling and pinning with its own lead word.
204	    static func voiceOverStem(at date: Date) -> String {
205	        let formatter = DateFormatter()
206	        formatter.locale = Locale(identifier: "en_US_POSIX")
207	        formatter.timeZone = .current
208	        formatter.dateFormat = "'Voice-over' yyyy-MM-dd 'at' HH.mm.ss"
209	        return formatter.string(from: date)
210	    }
211	
212	    /// `<stem>.<ext>` in `folder`, or `<stem> (2).<ext>`, `<stem> (3).<ext>`…
213	    /// while a file of that name exists — the Finder's own collision rule.
214	    static func uniqueURL(in folder: URL, stem: String, ext: String) -> URL {
215	        let manager = FileManager.default
216	        var candidate = folder.appendingPathComponent(stem).appendingPathExtension(ext)
217	        var counter = 2
218	        while manager.fileExists(atPath: candidate.path) {
219	            candidate = folder.appendingPathComponent("\(stem) (\(counter))")
220	                .appendingPathExtension(ext)
221	            counter += 1
222	        }
223	        return candidate
224	    }
225	
226	    /// The microphone's own file, beside the movie: the movie's stem plus
227	    /// ` (Microphone)`, as `.m4a` (R0 q6b: `AVCaptureAudioFileOutput` writes
228	    /// one mono 48 kHz AAC track there), made unique the same way.
229	    static func microphoneURL(beside movie: URL) -> URL {
230	        let stem = movie.deletingPathExtension().lastPathComponent + " (Microphone)"
231	        return uniqueURL(in: movie.deletingLastPathComponent(), stem: stem, ext: "m4a")
232	    }
233	
234	    /// Makes the folder, intermediate directories included. A folder that
235	    /// already exists is not an error.
236	    static func create(_ folder: URL) throws {
237	        try FileManager.default.createDirectory(
238	            at: folder, withIntermediateDirectories: true)
239	    }
240	}

244	/// The two ScreenCaptureKit configurations a choice becomes. PURE — every
245	/// field is set from the arguments and read back by the probe — which is
246	/// what lets the `excludesCurrentProcessAudio` mutant be caught at all: it
247	/// is invisible over MCP (nothing plays during a headless recording) and
248	/// this is the only row that sees it.
249	enum RecordingConfiguration {
250	    /// System audio is asked for at 48 kHz stereo, the rate the tap and
251	    /// `Loudness.swift` already assume of every file.
252	    static let sampleRate = 48_000
253	    static let channelCount = 2
254	
255	    /// `displayPointSize` and `scale` come from the caller, and the caller is
256	    /// `ScreenRecorder.start`, which reads them off the FILTER — its
257	    /// `contentRect` (points) and `pointPixelScale` — the one geometry
258	    /// source that also covers a picker-made filter (`SCDisplay`'s
259	    /// `width`/`height` are POINTS, R0 q4, and a display filter reports the
260	    /// display's point size and backing scale, a window filter the window's
261	    /// frame). The probe passes the numbers directly. `outputURL` is
262	    /// assigned before the output configuration is returned, and must stay
263	    /// so: reading `outputURL` off a fresh `SCRecordingOutputConfiguration`
264	    /// TRAPS (it imports non-optional and is nil underneath until assigned —
265	    /// the SDK scout's finding, exit 133).
266	    static func make(
267	        _ choice: RecordingChoice, displayPointSize: CGSize, scale: CGFloat, outputURL: URL
268	    ) -> (stream: SCStreamConfiguration, output: SCRecordingOutputConfiguration) {
269	        let stream = SCStreamConfiguration()
270	        // R0 q4: pixels are asked for, `.best` does not scale by itself.
271	        let factor: CGFloat = choice.resolution == .best ? max(scale, 1) : 1
272	        stream.width = Int((displayPointSize.width * factor).rounded())
273	        stream.height = Int((displayPointSize.height * factor).rounded())
274	        stream.captureResolution = choice.resolution == .best ? .best : .nominal
275	        stream.minimumFrameInterval = CMTime(value: 1, timescale: CMTimeScale(max(choice.rate, 1)))
276	        // CU-31: the pointer and its ring are the stream's only In the picture.
277	        let inPicture = choice.effectiveCursor == .inPicture
278	        stream.showsCursor = inPicture
279	        stream.showMouseClicks = choice.showClicks && inPicture
280	        // R0 q6a: the click circle draws only under BGRA; the default `420v`
281	        // is left alone when the stream draws no clicks, so an ordinary
282	        // recording's pixel path is byte for byte the spike's.
283	        if choice.showClicks && inPicture { stream.pixelFormat = REDACTED }
284	        stream.capturesAudio = choice.systemAudio
285	        stream.sampleRate = sampleRate
286	        stream.channelCount = channelCount
287	        // ALWAYS: the timeline can play while a recording runs and must not
288	        // be in it. `captureMicrophone` is deliberately never touched (R0
289	        // q2 — the microphone is a second file), so it keeps its default of
290	        // false, which the probe reads back on every row.
291	        stream.excludesCurrentProcessAudio = true
292	
293	        let output = SCRecordingOutputConfiguration()
294	        output.outputURL = outputURL
295	        output.outputFileType = .mov
296	        // R0 q2: `availableVideoCodecTypes` is `[avc1, hvc1]` here and the
297	        // default is `avc1`; HEVC halves the file where the encoder offers it.
298	        output.videoCodecType =
299	            output.availableVideoCodecTypes.contains(.hevc) ? .hevc : .h264
300	        return (stream, output)
301	    }
302	}

391	// An `extension ProjectDocument` in its own file, `+DisplayStem`'s shape: the
392	// base file is far over the ~600-line cap and takes no code it does not have

394	// `importSourceURL` are `private(set)` and `clampViewState()` is private, so
395	// an extension in another file cannot build the untitled document itself —
396	// and that method is `readMediaFile`'s post-probe body moved whole, so a
397	// recording becomes a document by the ONE spelling File ▸ Open uses for a

400	import AppKit

402	extension ProjectDocument {
403	    /// The untitled, dirty document a finished recording opens as — spec
404	    /// §1's opening flow for a movie, with two differences the recorder
405	    /// asks for. The CANVAS takes the recorder's rate (`choice.rate`, 30 or
406	    /// 60 — the grid the person chose) while the media record keeps the
407	    /// file's own, which for a ScreenCaptureKit file is whatever the screen
408	    /// did (R0 measured 25.58 fps at a 1/60 interval; decision 3). And the
409	    /// REMAINDER — a paused recording's later segments, back to back on the
410	    /// first one's track, and every microphone file on a new back track —
411	    /// lands through `RecordingLanding.remainderPlacement` as ONE grouped
412	    /// edit; the FIRST segment is what the document IS.
413	    ///
414	    /// **The order is a contract**, measured on the real class by the
415	    /// document scout and once more by the review, and each step leans on
416	    /// the one before:
417	    ///
418	    /// 1. `openUntitledDocumentAndDisplay(false)` — the controller ADDS the
419	    ///    document itself (no `addDocument`, or it is listed twice) and,
420	    ///    with `false`, makes no window yet.
421	    /// 2. `adoptImported` — with the first segment's descriptor, and BEFORE
422	    ///    anything reads `displayName`: AppKit pins the name on its first
423	    ///    read, and the name is `defaultDraftName()`, which is the
424	    ///    recording's stem only once `importSourceURL` is set. Nothing
425	    ///    between 1 and 2 logs, summarises or shows the document.
426	    /// 3. **The import count** — `fileModificationDate = nil` and
427	    ///    `countEditChange(.changeDone)`, the two lines `makeWindowControllers`
428	    ///    runs for an opened movie (`ProjectDocument.swift`, under its
429	    ///    `importSourceURL != nil, fileURL == nil, !isDocumentEdited` guard)
430	    ///    — run HERE, before the remainder's edit and with or without one.
431	    ///    The position is the fix for a defect the review measured on the
432	    ///    change count: counted the other way round, the remainder's edit
433	    ///    dirtied the document first, `makeWindowControllers`' guard found
434	    ///    it edited and skipped its own count, and ONE ⌘Z brought the count
435	    ///    back to zero — a recording's document that read CLEAN, which ⌘W
436	    ///    then closed without asking. Counted first, the remainder's edit
437	    ///    stacks a SECOND count and its undo leaves the first standing, so
438	    ///    the document is dirty with the remainder or without it, as an
439	    ///    opened movie is. Without a remainder this is the same one count
440	    ///    `makeWindowControllers` would have made, one step earlier.
441	    /// 4. The remainder's grouped edit — named by
442	    ///    `RecordingLanding.remainderActionName(for:)`: "Add Microphone"
443	    ///    for one segment with any voice — its own or a left-out segment's
444	    ///    (#181 item 2) — "Add Camera and Microphone" or "Add Camera" for
445	    ///    one segment with a camera beside the screen, with a voice or
446	    ///    without (spec §11 CAM-10 (4)), "Add Recording Segments" otherwise,
447	    ///    and NOT "Add Recording", because the step removes the remainder
448	    ///    and keeps the first segment's picture, and the Edit menu should
449	    ///    say what ⌘Z will do — before the window, so the `generateCaches()`
450	    ///    inside `makeWindowControllers` covers EVERY file and the editor's
451	    ///    first composition is built once, over the finished project, rather
452	    ///    than rebuilt when the later clips land. Every op was trialled
453	    ///    purely by `remainderPlacement`, so the windowless commit cannot
454	    ///    reach `presentError`'s app-modal arm.
455	    /// 5. `makeWindowControllers()` — its own import count is guarded out by
456	    ///    step 3 (the guard counts only a document nothing has counted, which
457	    ///    is what makes the two orders equivalent for a movie and step 3
458	    ///    safe here); what it still does is run `generateCaches()` and
459	    ///    `ensureReversedMedia()` and add the editor window.
460	    /// 6. `showWindows()`.
461	    ///
462	    /// A throw after step 1 CLOSES the document it opened, or a failed
463	    /// landing would leave an invisible untitled draft in the controller
464	    /// with a blank project in it.
465	    ///
466	    /// **Answers the document AND the remainder's `notes`** — the sentences
467	    /// `remainderPlacement` wrote for each file it landed as media with no
468	    /// clip (a voice too short for a frame, a voice wholly under the previous
469	    /// one, or everything behind a first picture the core refused), each
470	    /// naming the file. A document cannot show a note, and a landing that
471	    /// swallowed them would leave a person looking for a voice that is in the
472	    /// Media tab and nowhere on the timeline; the panel's note and the tool's
473	    /// `note` field append them. Empty when everything landed, and always
474	    /// empty with no remainder. A tuple rather than a property on the
475	    /// document because the notes are about ONE landing, not about the
476	    /// document, and the two callers read them exactly once.
477	    ///
478	    /// Two limits, recorded. With one segment and no microphone the document
479	    /// has NO undo step — its first project is what the document is, as for
480	    /// an opened movie — while with a remainder, ⌘Z (Undo Add Microphone, or
481	    /// Undo Add Recording Segments) removes the remainder's media and clips
482	    /// and leaves the first picture, and the document STAYS dirty under it
483	    /// (step 3's count): the first segment is the document, the rest is an
484	    /// edit to it. And every file stays on disk on either undo, as undoing
485	    /// Add Media… leaves the file (road map 3 §0). Main thread.
486	    static func untitled(around result: RecordingResult) throws
487	        -> (document: ProjectDocument, notes: [String])
488	    {
489	        assert(Thread.isMainThread)
490	        let controller = NSDocumentController.shared
491	        guard let document = try controller.openUntitledDocumentAndDisplay(false)
492	            as? ProjectDocument
493	        else {
494	            throw ReelCoreError(
495	                message: "The untitled document did not open as a Frame Job project.")
496	        }
497	        var notes: [String] = []
498	        do {
499	            try document.adoptImported(
500	                result.descriptor, source: URL(fileURLWithPath: result.descriptor.path),
501	                fps: Fps(num: result.choice.rate, den: 1))
502	            // Step 3: the import count, BEFORE the remainder's edit — see the
503	            // doc comment for why the order is the fix.
504	            document.fileModificationDate = nil
505	            document.countEditChange(.changeDone)
506	            if let remainder = try RecordingLanding.remainderPlacement(result, in: document) {
507	                document.performGroupedEdit(
508	                    RecordingLanding.remainderActionName(for: result), remainder.ops)
509	                notes = remainder.notes
510	            }
511	        } catch {
512	            document.close()
513	            throw error
514	        }
515	        document.makeWindowControllers()
516	        document.showWindows()
517	        return (document, notes)
518	    }
519	}

527	/// CO-81): Remove Background run over a finished recording's CAMERA clips as a follow-up to the
528	/// landing — never part of it — as its own undo step, "Remove Background", in AU-68's pattern
529	/// with no wait: the masks are wanted by the edit itself (`ensureMasks`, after every edit), so
530	/// nothing need be measured first. Both doors call `apply` right after the landing's commit and
531	/// before Enhance Voice and the polish (CU-101 (a)): the panel's two branches
532	/// (`RecorderPanelController+Landing.swift`) and the tool's `landAndEnhance`. On-device, so
533	/// never keyed (CJ-3). Names no `rc_*`; main thread.
534	enum RecordingCutout {
535	    /// The undo step's name, Clip ▸ Remove Background's.
536	    static let actionName = "Remove Background"
537	    /// The tool's `camera_cutout_error` when no camera clip took the cutout.
538	    static let noCameraSentence =
539	        "No camera clip landed on the timeline, so Remove Background did not run."
540	
541	    /// Every segment's camera file, in segment order; empty paths dropped, each path once. Pure.
542	    static func cameraPaths(of result: RecordingResult) -> [String] {
543	        var seen: Set<String> = []
544	        return result.segments.compactMap { $0.cameraDescriptor?.path }
545	            .map(RecordingLanding.trimmed)
546	            .filter { !$0.isEmpty && seen.insert($0).inserted }
547	    }

549	    /// Every clip of the open container whose media is one of `paths`, that can be cut out
550	    /// (`CutoutStatus.canCutOut`) and has no cutout yet, in id order. Main.
551	    static func cameraClips(_ paths: [String], in document: ProjectDocument) -> [UInt32] {
552	        let wanted = Set(paths)
553	        guard !wanted.isEmpty else { return [] }
554	        let snapshot = document.editedProject.snapshot
555	        return snapshot.clips.filter { clip in
556	            guard let media = snapshot.media(for: clip), wanted.contains(media.path) else {
557	                return false
558	            }
559	            return CutoutStatus.canCutOut(clip, in: snapshot) && clip.video?.cutout == nil
560	        }.map(\.id).sorted()
561	    }

563	    /// One base `set_video {cutout}` per clip, the whole default cutout, as Clip ▸ Remove
564	    /// Background writes. Pure over the ids.
565	    static func ops(_ clips: [UInt32], in document: ProjectDocument) -> [ReelOp] {
566	        clips.map { .setVideo(clips: [$0], patch: VideoPatch(cutout: .some(CutoutProps()))) }
567	    }

569	    /// When the recording's choice asks for it, its camera clips cut out as ONE grouped step
570	    /// "Remove Background" (`performGroupedEdit`: a landing is not an AppKit event). Answers the
571	    /// clips the step was asked for, empty when the choice did not ask or no camera clip
572	    /// qualifies (the panel is then quiet; the tool answers `noCameraSentence`). Main.
573	    @discardableResult static func apply(_ result: RecordingResult, in document: ProjectDocument)
574	        -> [UInt32]

576	        assert(Thread.isMainThread)
577	        guard result.choice.cameraCutout else { return [] }
578	        let clips = cameraClips(cameraPaths(of: result), in: document)
579	        guard !clips.isEmpty else { return [] }
580	        document.performGroupedEdit(actionName, ops(clips, in: document))

30	///   `ScreenRecorder`'s capture session instead.
31	/// - **`.best` does not scale by itself** (q4). `captureResolution = .best`
32	///   at the display's point size writes a point-sized file; pixels come only
33	///   when `width`/`height` are asked for in pixels, so `make` multiplies the
34	///   point size by the display's backing scale under `.best` itself.
35	/// - **Show Clicks needs BGRA** (q6a). `SCStream.h` says `showMouseClicks`
36	///   "currently applies when pixelFormat is set to BGRA" and a fresh
37	///   configuration reads `420v`, so `make` sets `REDACTED`
38	///   when the stream draws clicks and leaves the default alone otherwise —
39	///   measured, a recording output over a BGRA stream starts and writes. The
40	///   stream draws the pointer and its click ring only In the picture
41	///   (road map creator-jobs CU3c, spec §11 CU-31): with Separate, `make`
42	///   sets neither and keeps `420v`, and Show Clicks lands the screen clips
43	///   with ripples instead (`RecordingLanding+Cursor.swift`).
44	
45	// MARK: - The choice
46	
47	/// What is recorded. `.picked` is the panel's picker result, whose filter
48	/// is carried beside the choice (`ScreenRecorder.start` takes the filter as
49	/// its own argument), so the source enum never holds a framework object.
50	/// `.voiceOver` is the microphone alone, no picture (spec §11 recording, #99):
51	/// `ScreenRecorder.startVoiceOver` records it and `start` refuses it.
52	/// `.camera` is a camera alone, the device in `RecordingChoice.camera` (spec
53	/// §11 CAM-3): `ScreenRecorder.startCamera` records it and `start` refuses it,
54	/// while `start` records a camera beside a display, window or picked source (CAM-9).
55	enum RecordingSource: Equatable {
56	    case display(CGDirectDisplayID)
57	    case window(CGWindowID)
58	    case picked
59	    case voiceOver
60	    case camera
61	}
62	
63	/// `nominal` records the display's POINT size, `best` its pixel size
64	/// (`RecordingConfiguration.make` does the multiply — R0 q4).
65	enum RecordingResolution: String, CaseIterable {
66	    case nominal
67	    case best
68	}
69	
70	/// Where the recording lands when it stops. `.document` carries the target's
71	/// `recipeKey` rather than an `ObjectIdentifier`: an identifier of a closed
72	/// document is reused by the next one at the same address
73	/// (`RelinkSheetController.swift` says so), while a `recipeKey` is never
74	/// minted twice, so `RecordingLanding.resolve`'s miss → `.newProject`
75	/// fallback is exact.
76	enum RecordingDestination: Equatable {
77	    case newProject
78	    case document(recipeKey: Int)
79	}
80	
81	/// Which keys a screen recording writes into its cursor files (road map creator-jobs CU6,
82	/// spec §11 CU-60, CU-62): none, or each shortcut spelled and a time-only mark for every other
83	/// key-down, under Input Monitoring. An enum so a later mode needs no rename; `record_screen`'s
84	/// `keys` spells it.
85	enum RecordingKeys: String, CaseIterable {
86	    case off
87	    case shortcuts
88	}
89	
90	/// Where a screen recording's pointer goes (road map creator-jobs CU3c, spec §11 CU-31, CU-36):
91	/// `separate` — not in the movie, written to the cursor file for Frame Job to draw — or
92	/// `inPicture`, burned in by ScreenCaptureKit as before CU3c. `record_screen`'s `cursor` spells it.
93	enum RecordingCursor: String, CaseIterable {
94	    case separate
95	    case inPicture = "in_picture"
96	
97	    /// CU-36 (b), (c), amended at CU0d: a window or picked recording's default. The
98	    /// quiet-machine re-run of CU-S2's window rows settled their anchor as E1, so it is
99	    /// `.separate`, as a display's is.
100	    static let windowDefault: RecordingCursor = .separate
101	
102	    /// CU-36, amended at CU0d: `.separate` for a display, `windowDefault` (`.separate`) for a
103	    /// window or a picked source, and `.separate` for a voice-over or a camera alone, which have
104	    /// no pointer to draw.
105	    static func defaultFor(_ source: RecordingSource) -> RecordingCursor {
106	        switch source {
107	        case .display: return .separate
108	        case .window, .picked: return windowDefault
109	        case .voiceOver, .camera: return .separate
110	        }
111	    }
112	}
113	
114	/// Every control of the recorder panel and every argument of
115	/// `record_screen`, as one value. `microphone` is an
116	/// `AVCaptureDevice.uniqueID`, nil for off; `rate` is 30 or 60 (a camera
117	/// recording's is its format's, `CameraDevices.canvasRate`). `camera` is an
118	/// `AVCaptureDevice.uniqueID`, set with `source` `.camera`, or beside a
119	/// display, window or picked source (CAM-9), and `cameraFormat` its format
120	/// as `CameraDevices.spelled` writes it, nil for Best and set only with
121	/// `camera` (spec §11 CAM-6).
122	struct RecordingChoice: Equatable {
123	    var source: RecordingSource = .display(CGMainDisplayID())
124	    var includeFrameJobWindows: Bool = false
125	    var microphone: String? = nil
126	    var systemAudio: Bool = true
127	    var showClicks: Bool = false
128	    var rate: Int = 60
129	    var resolution: RecordingResolution = .nominal
130	    var destination: RecordingDestination = .newProject
131	    var folder: URL = RecordingFiles.folder()
132	    var camera: String? = nil
133	    var cameraFormat: String? = nil
134	    /// Enhance Voice on the voice's clips after the landing; only with a microphone (AU-68, AU-69).
135	    var enhanceMicrophone: Bool = false
136	    /// Record shortcuts (spec §11 CU-62): only with a display, window or picked source.
137	    var keys: RecordingKeys = .off
138	    /// The Cursor row (spec §11 CU-36): nil follows the source's default.
139	    var cursor: RecordingCursor? = nil
140	    /// The polish on landing (spec §11 CU-100…CU-102): Auto Zoom, Add Shortcut Overlays and
141	    /// Speed Up Typing over the landed screen clips, each its own undo step after the landing.
142	    var autoZoom: Bool = false
143	    var shortcutOverlays: Bool = false
144	    var speedUpTyping: Bool = false
145	    /// The camera beside the screen's layout and its cutout on landing (spec §11 CO-80…CO-82).
146	    var cameraLayout: RecordingCameraLayout = .cornerSquare
147	    var cameraCutout: Bool = false
148	
149	    /// The cursor this recording is made with: the choice, else the source's default.
150	    var effectiveCursor: RecordingCursor { cursor ?? .defaultFor(source) }
151	}
152	
153	// MARK: - Where the files go
154	
155	/// Decision 2 (road map 3 §0): a recording is ORIGINAL footage and lives in
156	/// `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/`, named by date and time — never in the
157	/// package (an untitled document has none) and never in the temporary
158	/// directory (where a cache is regenerable and footage would be lost). The
159	/// folder is created on demand, and `-RCRecordingFolder` overrides it the
160	/// way `-RCFFmpegPath` overrides the binary (`FFmpegRewrap.locate`), so a
161	/// proof can record into `tools/proof/work/` and delete it.
162	enum RecordingFiles {
163	    /// The launch-argument override, read from `UserDefaults.standard` so it
164	    /// works from the argument domain (`-RCRecordingFolder ~/x` on the
165	    /// command line, or a pinned volatile domain in a probe).
166	    static let folderDefaultsKey = "RCRecordingFolder"
167	
168	    /// The default folder's name under `~/Movies`.
169	    static let folderName = "Frame Job Recordings"
170	
171	    /// The folder a recording goes into: the override, tilde-expanded, when
172	    /// one is set; `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/` otherwise. Nothing is
173	    /// created here — `create(_:)` is called at the moment a recording has
174	    /// something to put in it, `AppSupport`'s rule.
175	    static func folder() -> URL {
176	        if let override = UserDefaults.standard.string(forKey: folderDefaultsKey),
177	            !override.isEmpty
178	        {
179	            return URL(
180	                fileURLWithPath: (override as NSString).expandingTildeInPath, isDirectory: true)
181	        }
182	        let movies =
183	            FileManager.default.urls(for: .moviesDirectory, in: .userDomainMask).first
184	            ?? FileManager.default.homeDirectoryForCurrentUser.appendingPathComponent(
185	                "Movies", isDirectory: true)
186	        return movies.appendingPathComponent(folderName, isDirectory: true)
187	    }
188	
189	    /// `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22` — the Screenshot app's
190	    /// spelling, in the machine's own time zone. The formatter is pinned to
191	    /// `en_US_POSIX` so a locale with another digit set or a 12-hour clock
192	    /// cannot change the name's shape; the seconds make a name unique across
193	    /// the app's own recordings and `uniqueURL` handles the rest.
194	    static func stem(at date: Date) -> String {
195	        let formatter = DateFormatter()
196	        formatter.locale = Locale(identifier: "en_US_POSIX")
197	        formatter.timeZone = .current
198	        formatter.dateFormat = "'Screen Recording' yyyy-MM-dd 'at' HH.mm.ss"
199	        return formatter.string(from: date)
200	    }
201	
202	    /// `Voice-over 2026-10-02 at 09.15.04` — a voice-over's file, `stem(at:)`'s
203	    /// spelling and pinning with its own lead word.
204	    static func voiceOverStem(at date: Date) -> String {
205	        let formatter = DateFormatter()
206	        formatter.locale = Locale(identifier: "en_US_POSIX")
207	        formatter.timeZone = .current
208	        formatter.dateFormat = "'Voice-over' yyyy-MM-dd 'at' HH.mm.ss"
209	        return formatter.string(from: date)
210	    }
211	
212	    /// `<stem>.<ext>` in `folder`, or `<stem> (2).<ext>`, `<stem> (3).<ext>`…
213	    /// while a file of that name exists — the Finder's own collision rule.
214	    static func uniqueURL(in folder: URL, stem: String, ext: String) -> URL {
215	        let manager = FileManager.default
216	        var candidate = folder.appendingPathComponent(stem).appendingPathExtension(ext)
217	        var counter = 2
218	        while manager.fileExists(atPath: candidate.path) {
219	            candidate = folder.appendingPathComponent("\(stem) (\(counter))")
220	                .appendingPathExtension(ext)
221	            counter += 1
222	        }
223	        return candidate
224	    }
225	
226	    /// The microphone's own file, beside the movie: the movie's stem plus
227	    /// ` (Microphone)`, as `.m4a` (R0 q6b: `AVCaptureAudioFileOutput` writes
228	    /// one mono 48 kHz AAC track there), made unique the same way.
229	    static func microphoneURL(beside movie: URL) -> URL {
230	        let stem = movie.deletingPathExtension().lastPathComponent + " (Microphone)"
231	        return uniqueURL(in: movie.deletingLastPathComponent(), stem: stem, ext: "m4a")
232	    }
233	
234	    /// Makes the folder, intermediate directories included. A folder that
235	    /// already exists is not an error.
236	    static func create(_ folder: URL) throws {
237	        try FileManager.default.createDirectory(
238	            at: folder, withIntermediateDirectories: true)
239	    }
240	}
241	
242	// MARK: - The configurations
243	
244	/// The two ScreenCaptureKit configurations a choice becomes. PURE — every
245	/// field is set from the arguments and read back by the probe — which is
246	/// what lets the `excludesCurrentProcessAudio` mutant be caught at all: it
247	/// is invisible over MCP (nothing plays during a headless recording) and
248	/// this is the only row that sees it.
249	enum RecordingConfiguration {
250	    /// System audio is asked for at 48 kHz stereo, the rate the tap and
251	    /// `Loudness.swift` already assume of every file.
252	    static let sampleRate = 48_000
253	    static let channelCount = 2
254	
255	    /// `displayPointSize` and `scale` come from the caller, and the caller is
256	    /// `ScreenRecorder.start`, which reads them off the FILTER — its
257	    /// `contentRect` (points) and `pointPixelScale` — the one geometry
258	    /// source that also covers a picker-made filter (`SCDisplay`'s
259	    /// `width`/`height` are POINTS, R0 q4, and a display filter reports the
260	    /// display's point size and backing scale, a window filter the window's
261	    /// frame). The probe passes the numbers directly. `outputURL` is
262	    /// assigned before the output configuration is returned, and must stay
263	    /// so: reading `outputURL` off a fresh `SCRecordingOutputConfiguration`
264	    /// TRAPS (it imports non-optional and is nil underneath until assigned —
265	    /// the SDK scout's finding, exit 133).
266	    static func make(
267	        _ choice: RecordingChoice, displayPointSize: CGSize, scale: CGFloat, outputURL: URL
268	    ) -> (stream: SCStreamConfiguration, output: SCRecordingOutputConfiguration) {
