402	extension ProjectDocument {
403	    /// The untitled, dirty document a finished recording opens as — spec
404	    /// §1's opening flow for a movie, with two differences the recorder
405	    /// asks for. The CANVAS takes the recorder's rate (`choice.rate`, 30 or
406	    /// 60 — the grid the person chose) while the media record keeps the
407	    /// file's own, which for a ScreenCaptureKit file is whatever the screen
408	    /// did (R0 measured 25.58 fps at a 1/60 interval; decision 3). And the
409	    /// REMAINDER — a paused recording's later segments, back to back on the
410	    /// first one's track, and every microphone file on a new back track —
411	    /// lands through `RecordingLanding.remainderPlacement` as ONE grouped
412	    /// edit; the FIRST segment is what the document IS.
413	    ///
414	    /// **The order is a contract**, measured on the real class by the
415	    /// document scout and once more by the review, and each step leans on
416	    /// the one before:
417	    ///
418	    /// 1. `openUntitledDocumentAndDisplay(false)` — the controller ADDS the
419	    ///    document itself (no `addDocument`, or it is listed twice) and,
420	    ///    with `false`, makes no window yet.
421	    /// 2. `adoptImported` — with the first segment's descriptor, and BEFORE
422	    ///    anything reads `displayName`: AppKit pins the name on its first
423	    ///    read, and the name is `defaultDraftName()`, which is the
424	    ///    recording's stem only once `importSourceURL` is set. Nothing
425	    ///    between 1 and 2 logs, summarises or shows the document.
426	    /// 3. **The import count** — `fileModificationDate = nil` and
427	    ///    `countEditChange(.changeDone)`, the two lines `makeWindowControllers`
428	    ///    runs for an opened movie (`ProjectDocument.swift`, under its
429	    ///    `importSourceURL != nil, fileURL == nil, !isDocumentEdited` guard)
430	    ///    — run HERE, before the remainder's edit and with or without one.
431	    ///    The position is the fix for a defect the review measured on the
432	    ///    change count: counted the other way round, the remainder's edit
433	    ///    dirtied the document first, `makeWindowControllers`' guard found
434	    ///    it edited and skipped its own count, and ONE ⌘Z brought the count
435	    ///    back to zero — a recording's document that read CLEAN, which ⌘W
436	    ///    then closed without asking. Counted first, the remainder's edit
437	    ///    stacks a SECOND count and its undo leaves the first standing, so
438	    ///    the document is dirty with the remainder or without it, as an
439	    ///    opened movie is. Without a remainder this is the same one count
440	    ///    `makeWindowControllers` would have made, one step earlier.
441	    /// 4. The remainder's grouped edit — named by
442	    ///    `RecordingLanding.remainderActionName(for:)`: "Add Microphone"
443	    ///    for one segment with any voice — its own or a left-out segment's
444	    ///    (#181 item 2) — "Add Camera and Microphone" or "Add Camera" for
445	    ///    one segment with a camera beside the screen, with a voice or
446	    ///    without (spec §11 CAM-10 (4)), "Add Recording Segments" otherwise,
447	    ///    and NOT "Add Recording", because the step removes the remainder
448	    ///    and keeps the first segment's picture, and the Edit menu should
449	    ///    say what ⌘Z will do — before the window, so the `generateCaches()`
450	    ///    inside `makeWindowControllers` covers EVERY file and the editor's
451	    ///    first composition is built once, over the finished project, rather
452	    ///    than rebuilt when the later clips land. Every op was trialled
453	    ///    purely by `remainderPlacement`, so the windowless commit cannot
454	    ///    reach `presentError`'s app-modal arm.
455	    /// 5. `makeWindowControllers()` — its own import count is guarded out by
456	    ///    step 3 (the guard counts only a document nothing has counted, which
457	    ///    is what makes the two orders equivalent for a movie and step 3
458	    ///    safe here); what it still does is run `generateCaches()` and
459	    ///    `ensureReversedMedia()` and add the editor window.
460	    /// 6. `showWindows()`.
461	    ///
462	    /// A throw after step 1 CLOSES the document it opened, or a failed
463	    /// landing would leave an invisible untitled draft in the controller
464	    /// with a blank project in it.
465	    ///
466	    /// **Answers the document AND the remainder's `notes`** — the sentences
467	    /// `remainderPlacement` wrote for each file it landed as media with no
468	    /// clip (a voice too short for a frame, a voice wholly under the previous
469	    /// one, or everything behind a first picture the core refused), each
470	    /// naming the file. A document cannot show a note, and a landing that
471	    /// swallowed them would leave a person looking for a voice that is in the
472	    /// Media tab and nowhere on the timeline; the panel's note and the tool's
473	    /// `note` field append them. Empty when everything landed, and always
474	    /// empty with no remainder. A tuple rather than a property on the
475	    /// document because the notes are about ONE landing, not about the
476	    /// document, and the two callers read them exactly once.
477	    ///
478	    /// Two limits, recorded. With one segment and no microphone the document
479	    /// has NO undo step — its first project is what the document is, as for
480	    /// an opened movie — while with a remainder, ⌘Z (Undo Add Microphone, or
481	    /// Undo Add Recording Segments) removes the remainder's media and clips
482	    /// and leaves the first picture, and the document STAYS dirty under it
483	    /// (step 3's count): the first segment is the document, the rest is an
484	    /// edit to it. And every file stays on disk on either undo, as undoing
485	    /// Add Media… leaves the file (road map 3 §0). Main thread.
486	    static func untitled(around result: RecordingResult) throws
487	        -> (document: ProjectDocument, notes: [String])
488	    {
489	        assert(Thread.isMainThread)
490	        let controller = NSDocumentController.shared
491	        guard let document = try controller.openUntitledDocumentAndDisplay(false)
492	            as? ProjectDocument
493	        else {
494	            throw ReelCoreError(
495	                message: "The untitled document did not open as a Frame Job project.")
496	        }
497	        var notes: [String] = []
498	        do {
499	            try document.adoptImported(
500	                result.descriptor, source: URL(fileURLWithPath: result.descriptor.path),
501	                fps: Fps(num: result.choice.rate, den: 1))
502	            // Step 3: the import count, BEFORE the remainder's edit — see the
503	            // doc comment for why the order is the fix.
504	            document.fileModificationDate = nil
505	            document.countEditChange(.changeDone)
506	            if let remainder = try RecordingLanding.remainderPlacement(result, in: document) {
507	                document.performGroupedEdit(
508	                    RecordingLanding.remainderActionName(for: result), remainder.ops)
509	                notes = remainder.notes
510	            }
511	        } catch {
512	            document.close()
513	            throw error
514	        }
515	        document.makeWindowControllers()
516	        document.showWindows()
517	        return (document, notes)
518	    }
519	}

content.content:
x
Records the screen for seconds and lands the movie as ORDINARY MEDIA — File ▸ New Recording…, without the panel. The file goes to ~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings (or the folder path names), named Screen Recording <date> at <time>.mov, and is then imported as import_media imports a file — a media entry — and, with place (the default), placed at the playhead on the front track of whatever container is open (inside a nest when set_scope has one open), or, when that track has no room there, on a new track in front of everything; a paused recording lands one clip per segment (below). With no project open, or when the target document closed while the recording ran, it opens as a NEW untitled project instead and landed says new_project; that document is then addressable by project: <the recording's path>, which is the path get_project reports for it. The canvas of that new project takes rate, while the media record keeps the file's OWN frame rate — for a screen recording that is whatever the screen did, since ScreenCaptureKit delivers a frame only when something changes, so a mostly-still screen reports a low, fractional fps; that is the file, not a defect, and the picture holds its last frame to the end of the sound. A microphone is a SECOND file (<stem> (Microphone).m4a) landing as a second clip on a new back track named Microphone, at the picture's start minus mic_offset — the measured lead of one file over the other, in ticks, positive meaning the picture began after the microphone; a negative start is the head trimmed, not a clip placed late. A microphone that never started, whose writer failed or whose file will not read does NOT fail the recording: the picture lands, that segment's mic_path and mic ids are absent, and mic_problem carries the sentence (the note repeats it). THE GRANTS: this tool never asks for one and never opens the picker. The Screen Recording grant (and the Microphone grant when microphone is true, and the Camera grant for source camera or a camera beside the screen) must already be held by this process — the panel is where somebody grants them — and a missing one is refused by name with the System Settings pane in the sentence. A Frame Job launched from a shell runs under the TERMINAL's grants, not the app icon's, and both refusals then also name the launching process (its pid) and the way out — relaunch with open -a "Frame Job", or grant the terminal. THE REFUSAL ORDER is fixed: your own mistakes first (seconds missing or outside 1…600, a source outside the vocabulary and the arguments that source refuses, display and window both given, a rate or size outside the vocabulary, enhance: true without a microphone and then with place: false, auto_zoom, shortcut_overlays and speed_up_typing each with place: false and the last two without keys: shortcuts, a camera_layout outside the vocabulary, camera_layout and then camera_cutout: true with place: false, microphone: true without the Microphone grant, a project naming nothing open), then for a camera recording or a camera beside the screen the camera lookup, then its camera_format, then the Camera grant, then for a screen recording the Screen Recording grant, then the display or window lookup — where a console that is locked or asleep lists NO display and is refused as that, by name; then the recording itself. While it records, a status item in the menu bar shows the elapsed time with a menu offering Pause Recording and Stop Recording — Resume Recording and Stop Recording while it is paused — and File ▸ Pause Recording (Resume Recording while paused) and File ▸ Stop Recording work too. A person's Stop from the menu bar or the File menu ends an agent's recording EARLY and it still lands, with stopped_by: stopped — the same value the tool's own stop at the span's end yields — and a duration shorter than the span, which is what says so; user_stopped is only the SYSTEM's own screen-recording indicator, and system_stopped a display that slept or a camera that stopped on its own. PAUSE: the span is wall clock, so a person's pause SHORTENS what the call records — the paused stretch is in no file — and the result's pauses says how many times Pause was pressed (0 when never; a pause with no resume before the stop still counts). A paused recording is a SEQUENCE of files, one per stretch between a start or resume and a pause or the stop, each named by its own start time and, with a microphone, carrying its own microphone file with its own measured mic_offset; every segment lands as its own clip placed at the previous one's end on ONE track, touching and never overlapping, and each microphone file as its own clip on the Microphone track at its own offset. segments carries one entry per file (exactly one for an unpaused recording) and duration is the TOTAL recorded across them. A segment whose movie will not read (an empty file, from a pause in the instant after a resume), or whose writer failed after the segment closed, is LEFT OUT rather than failing the recording: the readable segments land, and the result's unreadable lists each one left out — path, kept_files (what it left on disk), reason, and mic_path, mic_duration, mic_media and mic_clip when its microphone file reads, which lands without its picture in the slot the picture would have had — with the note naming them; only a recording with NO readable movie fails, naming every file. The call blocks for seconds plus about a second of start and finish, and up to 75 s more if the writers are slow to close the files — 60 s more for each further segment of a paused recording, whose files are probed in turn; a timeout names the movies, which may still finish on their own. THE RESULT carries: path (the FIRST segment's movie — the recording's file, the one a new project is addressed by); mic_offset (ALWAYS present — the first segment's, 0 without a microphone); mic_path and mic_duration (the first segment's) when its microphone file landed, and mic_problem — every segment's sentence, joine
keys {'enum': ['off', 'shortcuts'], 'type': 'string', 'description': "Which keys go into the recording's cursor files: off (default) or shortcuts — each shortcut pressed with cmd or ctrl, or with opt and an arrow, delete, forward delete, return, enter, tab or esc, spelled (cmd+shift+4), and a time-only mark for every other key, never which key was typed; nothing while an app holds secure input. Needs the Input Monitoring grant, which only the panel can ask for; without it the call is refused naming the System Settings pane. Refused with source voice_over and camera."}
show_clicks {'description': "Show each mouse click (default false). With cursor in_picture the stream draws a circle around each click into the movie; with cursor separate the recording's screen clips land with click ripples on (video.cursor.clicks ripple), drawn by Frame Job from the cursor file.", 'type': 'boolean'}
enhance {'type': 'boolean', 'description': "Run enhance_voice over the microphone's clips once they land and their sound is analysed, as its own undo step (default false); the answer gains enhance or enhance_error. Refused without microphone: true (or source voice_over), and with place: false."}
place {'type': 'boolean', 'description': "Put the clip (and the microphone's) on the timeline at the playhead (default true), in ONE undo step with the media. false adds the media to the list and no clip — import_media's shape — and the answer carries no clip or mic_clip id. For a NEW project the picture is the document, so its clips — one per segment, the first at 0 — are on the timeline whatever place says, and the answer notes it."}
speed_up_typing {'type': 'boolean', 'description': "Run speed_up_typing over the recording's screen clips last, once their speech is detected, as its own undo step Speed Up Typing (default false); the answer gains speed_up_typing or speed_up_typing_error. Refused with place: false, without keys: shortcuts, and with source voice_over and camera."}
path {'type': 'string', 'description': "A FOLDER to record into instead of ~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings, created if it does not exist. The file's name is always the dated one — this names the folder, never the file — and the answer's path is the file that was written. Trimmed; an empty or blank string means the default folder."}
shortcut_overlays {'type': 'boolean', 'description': "Run add_shortcut_overlays over the recording's screen clips after auto_zoom, as its own undo step Add Shortcut Overlays (default false); the answer gains shortcut_overlays or shortcut_overlays_error. Refused with place: false, without keys: shortcuts, and with source voice_over and camera."}
auto_zoom {'type': 'boolean', 'description': "Run auto_zoom over the recording's screen clips once they land, as its own undo step Auto Zoom (default false); the answer gains auto_zoom (auto_zoom's own answer) or auto_zoom_error. Refused with place: false, and with source voice_over and camera."}
cursor {'type': 'string', 'enum': ['separate', 'in_picture'], 'description': 'Where the pointer goes: separate — not in the movie; the cursor file records it and Frame Job draws it on the clip, where the Cursor section restyles it — or in_picture, burned into the movie by the system as before. Absent means separate. Refused with source voice_over and camera.'}

---
title: "Where a recording lands"
description: "Where a finished recording goes, into an open project at the playhead or as a new project of its own, what undo takes back, and when the panel comes back."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

When you stop, Frame Job adds the recording to your work without asking anything: into the project you chose, at its playhead, or as a new project. A recording is ordinary media from then on, so you can cut, move and delete its clips like any others.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
  keys="⌥⌘N"
  where="New Recording panel ▸ Record Into"
  tools={['record_screen', 'undo']}
/>

## Choose where it goes

**Record Into** on the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/) lists **New Project** and every open project. It follows whichever project is in front until you pick a row yourself, and it freezes when you press Record, so switching windows during a recording doesn't change where it goes.

While the files are written and imported, the panel's button reads **Stopping…** and then **Adding…**.

## Into an open project

The recording goes in at the chosen project's playhead, in whatever is open there. If you're working inside a [nest](/editing/nests/), it lands inside the nest.

| What was recorded | Where it lands |
| --- | --- |
| The picture, from a screen or a camera on its own | On the front track, when every stretch of it fits there. Otherwise all of it goes on a new track in front of everything. |
| The microphone | On a new back track named **Microphone**. |
| A [camera beside the screen](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/) | On a new track named **Camera**, in front of everything, in the panel's **Layout**. |
| A [voice-over](/recording/voice-overs/) | On a new back track named **Microphone**, from the playhead. |

A recording's picture is never split across two tracks. An existing Microphone track is never reused: each recording makes its own.

The microphone file and the movie don't start at quite the same moment, so Frame Job measures how far apart they began and places the microphone clip to match, trimming its head if it started first.

Every clip that landed is selected afterwards, microphone and camera clips included.

## Land a paused recording

Each [pause](/recording/pause-and-stop/) ends a file, so a paused recording is several files, one for each stretch. They land as one clip per stretch, back to back on one track. They touch, they never overlap, and no transition joins them. Each stretch's microphone file goes on the Microphone track, lined up with its own picture.

At a project frame rate that isn't a whole number, a gap of less than a frame can remain between two stretches.

## Undo a landing

Everything that lands in an open project is one undo step, **Add Recording**. **Edit ▸ Undo Add Recording** removes the clips and their media entries and leaves the files on disk, as undoing **Add Media…** does.

Anything set up in [When it lands](/recording/when-it-lands/) runs after the landing as its own undo steps, so those come off first.

## As a new project

With **Record Into** set to **New Project**, the recording opens in a new, untitled project named after its file, such as `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22`. That's the name Save offers.

The canvas takes the movie's size and the frame rate you chose in **Rate**, while the media keeps the file's own frame rate. Two sources differ:

- A [camera on its own](/recording/record-a-camera/) sets the canvas to the file's size at the camera format's frame rate.
- A voice-over has no picture, so the canvas is 1920×1080 at **Rate**, and later stretches follow the first on its one track.

The project is unsaved, and it asks before it closes.

The first stretch's picture is the project itself, so it has no undo step. Everything else that landed with it is one step, named for what it holds:

| What landed beside the first picture | Undo step |
| --- | --- |
| A microphone | **Add Microphone** |
| A camera | **Add Camera** |
| A camera and a microphone | **Add Camera and Microphone** |
| Later stretches, with or without a microphone or camera | **Add Recording Segments** |
| Only [click ripples](/recording/cursor/#show-clicks) | **Cursor Clicks** |
| Nothing | No step |

Undoing that step keeps the first picture, leaves the files on disk, and leaves the project unsaved.

## If you're dragging when it ends

If you're in the middle of a drag in the chosen project when the recording ends, the landing waits for the drag to finish, for up to 20 seconds. After that it gives up, and the panel's note reads "The recording was saved at … but could not be added: A drag was still in progress after 20 s." The files are on disk either way, and you can bring them in with **Add Media…**.

## If the chosen project closed

If the project you chose closes while you're recording, the recording opens as a new project instead, and the panel's note says "The document you chose was closed, so the recording opened as a new project."

## When the panel comes back

A recording that lands cleanly doesn't bring the panel back. Once it has landed, press <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd> to open it. While a recording runs, the same keys stop it.

The panel returns on its own, with a note, only if it was on screen when the recording began and there's something to report. The note can hold several of these at once.

| The note says | What happened |
| --- | --- |
| "Stopped from the system's screen-recording indicator; the recording was added." | You stopped it from macOS's own indicator, not from Frame Job. |
| "The system stopped the recording (the display slept or went away); what was captured was added." | The display slept or went away. See [When a recording stops on its own](/recording/when-a-recording-stops/). |
| "The camera stopped on its own. What was captured was added." | A camera recording ended because the camera stopped. The first sentence can give the camera's own reason instead. |
| "A segment was left out. … Its files are kept at …" | One stretch's movie couldn't be read, for example an empty file from a pause right after a resume. The other stretches landed. |
| "The left-out segment's microphone, …, was added to the project without its picture." | That stretch's microphone file was readable, so it's on the Microphone track where the picture would have been. The next picture starts after that gap. |
| A sentence about the microphone | It stopped or failed. The picture still landed. |
| A sentence about a resume | A resume failed. |
| "… is too short for a frame (… ms) and was added to the media list without a clip." | The file is in the Media tab, with nothing on the timeline. |
| "… was added to the media list without a clip: …" | The file couldn't be placed, and the sentence says why. |
| "The cursor file for … was not written: …" | That stretch has no [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/). |
| "The recording did not finish writing within 10 s." | The files didn't close within 10 seconds of the stop. The note names the files kept on disk. |
| "The recording was saved at … but could not be added: …" | Nothing landed. The note names every file, which are all on disk. |

## Good to know

- A project already at its limit of 64 tracks can't take a recording that needs a new track. The picture and the microphone land together or not at all, so if the picture would fit and the microphone wouldn't, nothing lands. The files stay on disk and the note names them.
- Only a recording with no readable movie at all fails, and its note names every file.
- When a stretch is left out, its camera file stays on disk and is named with its kept files, but it isn't added to the project.
- In a new project, a left-out first stretch's microphone goes to the media list with no clip, because the first readable picture starts the project at 0.

## With an agent

`record_screen` lands a recording the same way, with two differences. With no project open it always opens a new project. And it can add a recording to the media list without placing a clip, which the panel can't, though a new project's picture is on the timeline regardless. See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/).

## Related

- [The recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/)
- [Polish when a recording lands](/recording/when-it-lands/)
- [Recording files and formats](/recording/files-and-formats/)
- [When a recording stops on its own](/recording/when-a-recording-stops/)

---
title: "Polish when a recording lands"
description: "Tick boxes on the recorder panel to clean up the sound, zoom in on clicks, show shortcuts and speed up typing as soon as a recording lands."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

The boxes on the recorder panel run the clean-up you'd otherwise do by hand. The recording [lands](/recording/where-it-lands/) exactly as it would without them, and then each ticked box runs its command on what landed, each as its own undo step.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
  keys="⌥⌘N"
  where="New Recording panel ▸ When it lands:"
  tools={['record_screen', 'enhance_voice', 'auto_zoom', 'add_shortcut_overlays', 'speed_up_typing']}
  needs="Show shortcuts and Speed up typing need Record shortcuts, which needs macOS's Input Monitoring permission."
/>

<Shot
  name="16-recorder-panel.panel"
  alt="The New Recording panel. Under the Layout row, Remove the camera's background when it lands is greyed out. Under Microphone, Enhance the microphone when it lands is greyed out. Under When it lands, Zoom in on clicks is ticked, Show shortcuts is ticked and greyed out, and Speed up typing is unticked and greyed out."
/>

## Choose what runs

Tick the boxes on the panel before you press Record.

| Box | Runs | On | Default | Live when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Remove the camera's background when it lands** | **Clip ▸ Remove Background** | The camera's clips | Off | **Record the camera too** is ticked beside a display or a window |
| **Enhance the microphone when it lands** | **Clip ▸ Enhance Voice** | The microphone's clips | Off | A microphone is chosen, on any source |
| **Zoom in on clicks** | **Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…** | The screen clips | On | The source is a display or a window |
| **Show shortcuts** | **Clip ▸ Add Shortcut Overlays** | The screen clips | On | As above, with **Record shortcuts** ticked |
| **Speed up typing** | **Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…** | The screen clips | Off | As above, with **Record shortcuts** ticked |

A greyed box keeps its value for next time, and every box is greyed while a recording is under way. The panel remembers all five between uses.

The screen clips are the clips of each stretch's movie that has a [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/). No other clip is touched, and a voice-over or a camera on its own has none.

:::note
**Zoom in on clicks** is on from the start, so a display or window recording lands with zooms unless you untick it. **Show shortcuts** is on too, but it does nothing until you tick [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/), which is off.
:::

## The order they run in

The steps always run in this order, whichever you tick:

1. **Remove Background**, straight after the landing.
2. **Enhance Voice**, once the sound has been analysed.
3. **Auto Zoom**.
4. **Add Shortcut Overlays**.
5. **Speed Up Typing**, once the speech has been detected.

Each is its own undo step, named as above, and they all come after the landing's. **Edit ▸ Undo** takes them off one at a time, last first, and keeps the recording.

The order matters. Zooms are planned on whole clips before the speed-up splits them, and the speed-up leaves each overlay at its pace.

Each command uses the settings its own menu command would, and only Enhance Voice shows a sheet. Nothing asks you a question.

## Enhance the microphone

**Enhance the microphone when it lands** runs [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) on each stretch's microphone file, or on a voice-over's files. It never touches the picture, a camera or the system audio.

Enhance Voice needs the sound's loudness and speech analysed first, which takes a few seconds after the files land. It then runs under the **Measuring Sound** sheet, at the target loudness of the [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) row, and its settings appear in the clip's [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/).

Choosing **Cancel** on the sheet leaves the clips as they landed.

**Edit ▸ Undo Enhance Voice** takes the processing off and keeps the recording. In an open project the next undo is **Add Recording**. In a new project it's the landing's own step, such as **Add Microphone**, or nothing when the recording is a single file.

If a second recording lands in the same project while the first is still waiting, its clips join the wait and the wait starts again.

## Zoom in on clicks

**Zoom in on clicks** runs [Auto Zoom](/recording/auto-zoom/) with the values the Auto Zoom sheet last used. **Zoom on typing** is turned on when the recording has typing, and off when it hasn't.

## Show shortcuts

**Show shortcuts** runs [Add Shortcut Overlays](/recording/shortcut-overlays/) with its usual settings: at the bottom of the picture, in the dark theme.

## Speed up typing

**Speed up typing** runs [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/) with the values its sheet last used. It waits until the speech has been detected, so typing you talk over keeps its pace.

A speed-up that would leave a clip silent above ×12 is never applied here, because the panel can't ask you first. The foot of the inspector says so instead. Choose **Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…** yourself to be asked. See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).

## What the steps wait for

Enhance Voice, Auto Zoom, Add Shortcut Overlays and Speed Up Typing each hold off while:

- you're dragging in the project
- a sheet is up on its window
- you're inside a different nest from the one the recording landed in

They carry on by themselves once that's over. Each gets up to 5 minutes, counted from when the step before it finished, and Auto Zoom's starts when Enhance Voice is done.

## When a step can't run

A problem shows at the foot of the [inspector](/getting-started/the-window/), with no beep and no sheet. A step with nothing to do says nothing at all: a recording with no cursor file, a recording with no microphone clip, or no click, shortcut or typing stretch long enough changes nothing and shows no message.

| The inspector says | What happened | What runs next |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "Enhance Voice did not run on the recording: its microphone was not ready to measure within 5 minutes. Select its clip and choose Clip ▸ Enhance Voice." | The sound wasn't analysed in time, or the project stayed busy. | The other steps |
| "Nothing could be enhanced. …" | There was nothing to measure, for example a silent microphone. The sentence gives the reason. | The other steps |
| "… did not run on the recording: the project was busy for 5 minutes. Select its clips and choose Clip ▸ …" | You were dragging, a sheet was up, or you were in another nest for the whole wait. | Nothing. Run the rest yourself. |
| "Speed Up Typing did not run on the recording: its speech was not detected within 5 minutes. Select its clips and choose Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…." | Speech detection didn't finish in time. | It's the last step. |
| "Clip … now plays above ×12, so its audio is left out: it is silent in the preview and the export." | The speed-up would do this, so it was left off. Despite the wording, nothing changed. | It's the last step. |
| Any other sentence | The command wouldn't run. This is the sentence it would show from its own menu item. | The next step |

A cursor file that can't be read is reported the same way, and the steps after it don't run.

## With an agent

`record_screen` can run the same steps, with some differences:

- Every step is off unless the agent asks for it, **Zoom in on clicks** included.
- Enhance Voice runs at −16 LUFS, not at the Normalize row's target. The agent can call `enhance_voice` afterwards for another target.
- The other steps use the tools' own defaults, never the values a sheet remembers.
- A speed-up that leaves a clip silent above ×12 is applied, and the agent is told.

See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/).

- [Shortcut overlays](/recording/shortcut-overlays/)
- [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/)

---
title: "Recording files and formats"
description: "Where recordings are saved, how their files are named, what format each one is, and why a still screen gives a low frame rate."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Every recording is a set of ordinary files in one folder, so they outlast any project they land in. This page lists what each recording writes and in what format.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
  keys="⌥⌘N"
  tools="record_screen"
/>

## Where recordings are saved

Recordings go in `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/`, which Frame Job creates the first time it needs it. The panel's footnote shows the folder before you start.

They're never stored inside the project package. A recording is original footage, so it survives even if you never save the project it opened in, and undoing a landing leaves its files on disk. To carry recordings into the package, use [Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/).

## What each recording writes

| File | Example name | Format |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Screen movie](#the-screen-movie) | `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22.mov` | QuickTime movie, HEVC or H.264 |
| [Its microphone](#the-microphone-file) | `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22 (Microphone).m4a` | Mono 48 kHz AAC |
| [Its cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/) | `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22.fjcursor` | Frame Job's own |
| [Voice-over](#voice-over-files) | `Voice-over 2026-10-02 at 09.15.04.m4a` | Mono 48 kHz AAC |
| [Camera on its own](#camera-files) | `Camera Recording 2026-10-26 at 17.14.33.mov` | QuickTime movie, HEVC or H.264 |
| [Camera beside the screen](#camera-files) | `Screen Recording 2026-10-26 at 17.14.33 (Camera).mov` | QuickTime movie, HEVC or H.264 |

## How files are named

A file is named by the date and time it began, on a 24-hour clock in your Mac's time zone.

A [pause](/recording/pause-and-stop/) ends a file and a resume starts a new one, so each stretch of a paused recording is its own set of files, named by the time that stretch began.

When a name is already taken, Frame Job adds ` (2)`, ` (3)` and so on.

## The screen movie

A screen recording is a QuickTime `.mov` in HEVC where your Mac offers it, otherwise H.264. Its size comes from the panel's **Size** row, or a picked window's own size.

With **System Audio** on, the movie has one stereo 48 kHz sound track of what your Mac plays. Frame Job's own sound is left out, so playing your timeline during a recording doesn't get into it.

The microphone is never a track of the movie.

## The microphone file

The microphone is written beside the movie, named after it with ` (Microphone)` added, as one mono 48 kHz AAC track.

Keeping it apart from the system sound means you can set the level of your voice and your computer's sound separately. See [System audio and the microphone](/recording/system-audio-and-microphone/).

## Voice-over files

A [voice-over](/recording/voice-overs/) is a mono 48 kHz AAC `.m4a` named `Voice-over <date> at <time>.m4a`, one file for each stretch between pauses.

## Camera files

A camera recording is a QuickTime `.mov` at the camera's format, in HEVC where that can be used at the format's size, otherwise H.264. It has no sound of its own.

- A [camera on its own](/recording/record-a-camera/) is named `Camera Recording <date> at <time>.mov`.
- A [camera beside the screen](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/) is named after the screen movie with ` (Camera)` added, one for each stretch.

Any microphone file sits beside the movie, named as for a screen recording.

## Why a still screen gives a low frame rate

macOS delivers a new frame only when something on screen changes, so a mostly still screen gives a file with a low, uneven frame rate. That rate comes from the file itself and isn't a fault. The picture holds until the next change.

**Rate**, 30 or 60 fps, is the most frames per second the file can hold. A new project uses it as its frame rate, while the media entry keeps the file's real rate.

Where the picture stops changing before the sound ends, the last frame is held to the end of the clip.

## With an agent

An agent can record into another folder, created if it's missing, which the panel can't. It names the folder only: the file always takes its dated name. See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/).

## Related

- [Where a recording lands](/recording/where-it-lands/)
- [Cursor files](/recording/cursor-files/)
- [Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/)
- [Project frame rate](/projects/frame-rate/)

---
title: "The cursor in a recording"
description: "Choose whether the pointer is kept out of a screen recording for Frame Job to draw, or drawn into the movie by macOS, and how clicks are shown."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A screen recording can keep the pointer out of the movie, so Frame Job draws it on the clip and you can restyle it later, or have macOS draw it into the picture for good. You choose before you record, because the choice is part of the movie.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
  keys="⌥⌘N"
  where={['New Recording panel ▸ Cursor', 'New Recording panel ▸ Show Clicks']}
  tools="record_screen"
/>

## Choose Separate or In the picture

Set **Cursor** on the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/).

| | **Separate** | **In the picture** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The pointer | Kept out of the movie. Frame Job draws it on the clip. | Drawn into the movie by macOS. |
| Restyle it later | Yes, in the clip's **Cursor** section. | No. It can't be changed or removed. |
| **Show Clicks** | Click ripples, drawn by Frame Job. | A ring drawn into the movie. |
| The **Cursor** section | Appears on the clip. | Doesn't appear. |
| Cursor file | Written | Written |

**Cursor** is greyed out, keeping its value, with **Camera** or **Microphone Only** as the source, and while a recording is under way.

**Show Clicks** marks each mouse click. It's off by default, and greyed out with **Camera** or **Microphone Only**.

- **With Separate**, nothing is drawn into the movie. Frame Job draws the ripples from the cursor file, and you can edit them afterwards.

The pointer is in the movie and the cursor file says so, so the clip shows no **Cursor** section and nothing is drawn twice.

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

```mdx
## Add a marker

```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.
